name: Imperial State of Iran
description: The Imperial State of Iran emerged on 15 December 1925 following the formal deposition of the Qajar dynasty by the national constituent assembly, which elevated Prime Minister Reza Khan to the throne as Reza Shah Pahlavi. Centred upon the capital of Tehran, the monarchical state pursued rigorous administrative centralisation, secular legal restructuring and rapid industrial modernisation across the Iranian plateau. The realm endured Anglo-Soviet military occupation during the Second World War, after which Mohammad Reza Pahlavi presided over an autocratic modernisation drive until the Iranian Revolution dissolved the monarchy in 1979. \n\n Status: Sovereign monarchy; Capital: Tehran; Official languages: Persian; Religion: Shia Islam; Government: Unitary semi-constitutional monarchy; Ruling dynasty: Pahlavi dynasty; Ruler title: Shah; Historical era: Interwar and Cold War; Preceded by: Qajar Iran; Succeeded by: Islamic Republic of Iran

name: Kingdom of Hejaz and Sultanate of Nejd
description: The Kingdom of Hejaz and Sultanate of Nejd constituted a dual monarchy established under British protection following Abdulaziz ibn Saud's successful conquest of the Hashemite realm in western Arabia. Governed from Riyadh, the composite regime maintained separate administrative mechanisms for the coastal Hejaz and the interior Nejd while managing crucial pilgrimage routes to Mecca and Medina. The entity remained subject to British political guidance until the 1927 Treaty of Jeddah recognised full Saudi sovereignty, paving the way for eventual peninsular unification. \n\n Status: British protectorate; Capital: Riyadh; Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Islamic absolute monarchy; Ruling dynasty: House of Saud; Ruler title: King of Hejaz and Sultan of Nejd; Historical era: Interwar period; Preceded by: Kingdom of Hejaz; Succeeded by: Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd

name: Lebanese Republic
description: The Lebanese Republic took form on 23 May 1926 when the French mandatory authorities in the Levant promulgated a constitutional framework transforming the State of Greater Lebanon into an autonomous parliamentary republic. Headquartered in the coastal port city of Beirut, the administration institutionalised a delicate confessional power-sharing system among Maronite Christians, Sunni Muslims, Shia Muslims and other sectarian communities. France exercised supreme political and military oversight over Lebanese external affairs through a high commissioner until full independence was realised in 1946. \n\n Status: League of Nations mandate; Capital: Beirut; Common languages: Arabic and French; Religion: Christianity and Islam; Government: Parliamentary republic under confessionalism; Ruler title: High Commissioner; Historical era: Interwar period; Preceded by: State of Greater Lebanon; Succeeded by: Lebanese Republic

name: Portuguese Republic
description: The Portuguese Republic entered an authoritarian phase on 28 May 1926 when a right-wing military coup d'état brought an end to the turbulent First Portuguese Republic. Governed from Lisbon, the newly instituted National Dictatorship suspended constitutional liberties, curbed parliamentary opposition and suppressed republican insurrections across the mainland and overseas dominions. The military junta struggled to resolve deep structural economic crises until financial director António de Oliveira Salazar consolidated political authority, facilitating the promulgation of the corporatist Estado Novo in 1933. \n\n Status: Military dictatorship; Capital: Lisbon; Official languages: Portuguese; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Unitary republic under military rule; Head of state: President; Historical era: Interwar period; Preceded by: First Portuguese Republic; Succeeded by: Portuguese Republic; Currency: Portuguese escudo

name: Kingdom of Afghanistan
description: The Kingdom of Afghanistan was established on 9 June 1926 when King Amanullah Khan elevated the former Barakzai emirate into a fully sovereign monarchy governed from Kabul. The realm initiated ambitious legal, educational and administrative modernisations across Central Asia, though reactionary tribal rebellions briefly unseated the royal government in 1929 before King Mohammed Nadir Shah restored order. Afghanistan maintained armed neutrality through international conflicts and operated under a parliamentary constitution from 1964 until a republican coup dissolved the crown in 1973. \n\n Status: Sovereign monarchy; Capital: Kabul; Official languages: Pashto and Dari; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Unitary constitutional monarchy; Ruling dynasty: Barakzai dynasty; Ruler title: King; Historical era: Interwar and Cold War; Preceded by: Emirate of Afghanistan; Succeeded by: Republic of Afghanistan

name: Republic of China
description: The Republic of China functioned under the one-party tutelage of the Kuomintang nationalist party following Chiang Kai-shek's successful Northern Expedition against rival northern warlords. Administered from its primary capital at Nanjing, the central government sought to integrate fractured regional provinces while combating persistent insurrections by communist forces. The nationalist regime endured devastating territorial losses during the Second Sino-Japanese War and subsequent civil war warfare, ultimately relocating its administrative apparatus to Taiwan in December 1949. \n\n Status: Sovereign republic; Capital: Nanjing; Official languages: Standard Chinese; Government: One-party republic under military tutelage; Head of state: Chairman of the National Government; Historical era: Interwar and World War II; Preceded by: Beiyang government; Succeeded by: People's Republic of China; Currency: Chinese yuan

name: Idrisid Emirate of Asir
description: The Idrisid Emirate of Asir was an autonomous traditional polity situated along the southern Red Sea littoral of the Arabian Peninsula, administered from its historic seat at Sabya. Threatened by expansionist incursions from the neighbouring Kingdom of Yemen, Emir al-Hasan ibn Ali entered into the Treaty of Mecca in October 1926, which placed the territory under Saudi suzerainty. Although local authority initially remained with the Idrisid dynasty, rising discontent culminated in an aborted uprising that prompted direct military annexation by Saudi Arabia in 1934. \n\n Status: Protectorate; Capital: Sabya; Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Islamic hereditary principality; Ruling dynasty: Idrisid dynasty; Ruler title: Emir; Historical era: Interwar period; Succeeded by: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia

name: Albanian Republic
description: The Albanian Republic was established on 31 January 1925 under the leadership of President Ahmet Zogu, who consolidated dictatorial control from the capital city of Tirana. Hemmed in by territorial rivalries with Yugoslavia and Greece, the fledgling Balkan republic entered into the comprehensive Treaties of Tirana with Fascist Italy in November 1926, relinquishing significant economic and military autonomy. Italian loans and military instructors effectively turned the state into a Rome-dominated protectorate before Zogu transformed the polity into a personal monarchy in 1928. \n\n Status: Italian protectorate; Capital: Tirana; Official languages: Albanian; Religion: Islam and Christianity; Government: Parliamentary republic under authoritarian rule; Head of state: President; Historical era: Interwar period; Preceded by: Principality of Albania; Succeeded by: Kingdom of Albania; Currency: Albanian franga

name: Spanish Territories of the Gulf of Guinea
description: The Spanish Territories of the Gulf of Guinea formed a unified colonial possession administered by the Spanish Crown along the western coast of equatorial Africa and adjacent oceanic islands. Centred administratively at Santa Isabel on the island of Fernando Po, the colony encompassed continental Rio Muni together with Annobon, Corisco and the Elobey Islands. The colonial government exploited lucrative cocoa and timber concessions while maintaining tight paternalistic controls over indigenous Fang and Bubi populations until granting complete national independence as Equatorial Guinea in 1968. \n\n Status: Colony of Spain; Administrative seat: Santa Isabel; Official languages: Spanish; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Colonial governor-generalship; Ruler title: Governor-General; Historical era: New Imperialism and Cold War; Succeeded by: Republic of Equatorial Guinea; Currency: Spanish peseta

name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
description: The United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland assumed its modern constitutional designation on 12 April 1927 following the formal establishment of the Irish Free State and the Royal and Parliamentary Titles Act. Centred upon the imperial capital of London, the unitary parliamentary monarchy governed England, Scotland, Wales and the six north-eastern counties of Ireland alongside a sweeping worldwide empire. The state played an indispensable leadership role across the Second World War and subsequently guided the decolonisation of its overseas dependencies into the Commonwealth of Nations. \n\n Status: Sovereign constitutional monarchy; Capital and largest city: London; Official languages: English; Religion: Christianity; Government: Unitary parliamentary constitutional monarchy; Ruling dynasty: House of Windsor; Head of state: Monarch; Legislature: Parliament; Currency: Pound sterling

name: Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd
description: The Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd was a fully sovereign dual monarchy founded on 20 May 1927 when the Treaty of Jeddah formally nullified British protectorate oversight. Ruled from Riyadh by King Abdulaziz ibn Saud, the composite state joined the vast central desert plateau of Nejd with the historic coastal province of Hejaz under a single sovereign crown. Separate administrative and legal apparatuses were maintained across the two realms until September 1932, when royal decree unified all royal territories into the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. \n\n Status: Sovereign monarchy; Capital: Riyadh; Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Islamic absolute monarchy; Ruling dynasty: House of Saud; Ruler title: King; Historical era: Interwar period; Preceded by: Kingdom of Hejaz and Sultanate of Nejd; Succeeded by: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia

name: Republic of Ararat
label: modern kurdish polities
description: The Republic of Ararat was a self-declared Kurdish breakaway state established on 28 October 1927 amidst an extensive regional uprising in south-eastern Anatolia against Turkish national authority. Guided by the Xoybun nationalist committee from its mountain stronghold at Kurd Ava near Mount Ararat, the provisional administration established rudimentary civilian institutions, maintained active military regiments and appealed for international diplomatic recognition. The fledgling republic resisted several Turkish military operations before being decisively crushed and reincorporated into the Republic of Turkey in late 1930. \n\n Status: Unrecognised state; Capital: Kurd Ava; Common languages: Kurdish; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Revolutionary republic; Head of state: President; Historical era: Interwar period; Preceded by: Republic of Turkey; Succeeded by: Republic of Turkey; Historical region: Eastern Anatolia

name: Bouvet Island
description: Bouvet Island is an uninhabited, glacier-covered volcanic island in the South Atlantic Ocean that was formally annexed as a dependent territory of Norway on 23 January 1928. Located along the southern Mid-Atlantic Ridge far north of the Antarctic Treaty zone, the remote landmass possesses no permanent harbour or civilian settlement and is governed directly from Oslo. Norwegian authorities have designated the entire island as a nature reserve, maintaining an automated meteorological research station on its rugged western coast at Nyroysa. \n\n Status: External dependency; Administrative seat: Oslo; Common languages: Norwegian; Government: Uninhabited dependent territory; Head of state: Monarch of Norway; Historical era: Interwar to present; Preceded by: Terra nullius; Succeeded by: Kingdom of Norway

name: Kingdom of Albania
description: The Kingdom of Albania was proclaimed on 1 September 1928 when President Ahmet Zogu assumed the royal mantle as King Zog I, governing the mountainous Balkan territory from Tirana. Although legally constituted as an independent constitutional monarchy, the kingdom functioned as a de facto Italian protectorate bound by onerous economic concessions and extensive military agreements. Rising friction between Zog and Italian dictator Benito Mussolini over national sovereignty eventually provoked a full-scale Italian military invasion in April 1939, extinguishing Albanian domestic autonomy. \n\n Status: Italian protectorate; Capital: Tirana; Official languages: Albanian; Religion: Islam and Christianity; Government: Constitutional monarchy under authoritarian rule; Ruling dynasty: House of Zogu; Ruler title: King; Historical era: Interwar period; Preceded by: Albanian Republic; Succeeded by: Kingdom of Albania; Currency: Albanian franga

name: Emirate of Afghanistan
description: The Emirate of Afghanistan emerged during the tumultuous Afghan Civil War on 12 December 1928 when Tajik rebel chieftain Habibullah Kalakani launched an armed uprising against royal reform programmes. Operating from northern bases before capturing Kabul in January 1929, the insurgent Saqqawist regime abolished modernising secular decrees and instituted strict traditional Islamic governance. The unrecognised emirate held power for ten turbulent months until royalist forces commanded by General Mohammed Nadir Khan ousted Kalakani and re-established the Barakzai monarchy in October 1929. \n\n Status: Revolutionary rebel regime; Capital: Kabul; Common languages: Dari and Pashto; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Traditional Islamic emirate; Ruler title: Emir; Historical era: Interwar period; Preceded by: Kingdom of Afghanistan; Succeeded by: Kingdom of Afghanistan

name: Vatican City State
description: Vatican City State was established on 7 June 1929 through the ratification of the Lateran Treaty between the Holy See and the Kingdom of Italy, resolving decades of diplomatic contention following the 1870 capture of Rome. Occupying an ecclesiastical enclave on Vatican Hill within Rome, the tiny microstate provides an independent sovereign territorial base for the universal government of the Catholic Church. The polity functions as an absolute elective monarchy headed by the Bishop of Rome, who exercises supreme executive, legislative and judicial power. \n\n Status: Sovereign ecclesiastical state; Capital and largest city: Vatican City; Official languages: Italian and Latin; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Theocratic elective absolute monarchy; Head of state: Pope; Legislature: Pontifical Commission; Currency: Euro; Historical era: Interwar to present

name: Kingdom of Yugoslavia
description: The Kingdom of Yugoslavia was formally proclaimed on 3 October 1929 when King Alexander I renamed the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes and instituted an autocratic royal dictatorship from Belgrade. Divided into nine administrative banovinas that ignored traditional historic frontiers, the centralised monarchy sought to forge an integral Yugoslav national identity while suppressing ethnic separatism. The state endured chronic political friction, the assassination of Alexander in 1934 and severe internal strain until the Axis invasion of April 1941 dismantled the country. \n\n Status: Sovereign monarchy; Capital: Belgrade; Official languages: Serbo-Croato-Slovene; Religion: Eastern Orthodoxy, Roman Catholicism and Sunni Islam; Government: Unitary royal dictatorship; Ruling dynasty: Karadordevic dynasty; Ruler title: King; Historical era: Interwar period; Preceded by: Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes; Currency: Yugoslav dinar

name: Chinese Communist Party
description: The Chinese Communist Party maintained autonomous insurgent territorial bases across revolutionary enclaves in southern, central and north-western China while prosecuting a prolonged armed struggle against the Nationalist government. Centred initially at the Jiangxi Soviet capital of Ruijin before undertaking the Long March to Yan'an in Shaanxi, the party organised agrarian soviets, enforced land redistribution and built the formidable Red Army. Party chairman Mao Zedong mobilised rural peasant support throughout the anti-Japanese conflict and civil war, culminating in the proclamation of the People's Republic in 1949. \n\n Status: Revolutionary insurgent state; Administrative seat: Ruijin and Yanan; Common languages: Standard Chinese; Religion: State atheism; Government: Communist one-party soviet republic; Head of state: Chairman of the Central Executive Committee; Historical era: Interwar and World War II; Succeeded by: People's Republic of China; Currency: Soviet yuan

name: Syrian Republic
description: The Syrian Republic was proclaimed on 14 May 1930 under a French-promulgated constitution that transformed the mandatory State of Syria into a parliamentary republic administered from Damascus. The fledgling polity witnessed ceaseless political friction between French mandatory officials and Syrian nationalist blocs striving for full sovereignty, the integration of autonomous Alawite and Druze regions and the preservation of Alexandretta. Although local authorities negotiated a treaty of independence in 1936, France maintained military and diplomatic hegemony across the Levant until the complete evacuation of foreign troops in April 1946. \n\n Status: League of Nations mandate; Capital: Damascus; Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Islam and Christianity; Government: Parliamentary republic under French mandate; Ruler title: High Commissioner; Historical era: Interwar and World War II; Preceded by: State of Syria; Succeeded by: Syrian Republic; Currency: Syrian pound

name: Liugong Island Concession
label: concessions in china
description: The Liugong Island Concession was a strategic British leased naval territory situated at the entrance of Weihaiwei Bay off the north-eastern coast of Shandong Province. When Great Britain returned the wider Weihaiwei territory to the Republic of China on 1 October 1930, it secured a ten-year lease over Liugong Island to maintain a dedicated anchorage and summer naval coaling base for the Royal Navy China Station. British naval personnel occupied barracks and maritime installations across the island until Japanese forces occupied the area upon the expiration of the leasehold in 1940. \n\n Status: British naval concession; Administrative seat: None (Royal Navy station); Common languages: English and Standard Chinese; Government: Military naval administration; Ruler title: Commander-in-Chief, China Station; Historical era: Interwar period; Preceded by: British Weihaiwei; Succeeded by: Republic of China; Historical region: Shandong

name: Catalan Republic
description: The Catalan Republic was proclaimed in Barcelona on 14 April 1931 by republican leader Francesc Macia amidst the revolutionary collapse of the Spanish Bourbon monarchy. Declared as an independent component within an envisioned Iberian confederation, the provisional government exercised authority over Catalonia for only three days before conducting intensive negotiations with ministers of the newly established Second Spanish Republic. In exchange for significant regional self-rule under the re-established Generalitat of Catalonia, Macia agreed to dissolve the separate republican state and integrate Catalonia into democratic Spain. \n\n Status: Short-lived unrecognised republic; Capital: Barcelona; Official languages: Catalan and Spanish; Religion: Secular; Government: Provisional republic; Head of state: President; Historical era: Interwar period; Preceded by: Kingdom of Spain; Succeeded by: Generalitat of Catalonia; Historical region: Catalonia

name: Spanish Republic
description: The Spanish Republic, known retrospectively as the Second Spanish Republic, was proclaimed on 14 April 1931 following municipal elections that prompted the abdication and exile of King Alfonso XIII. Headquartered in Madrid, the democratic regime enacted far-reaching secularisation laws, initiated sweeping agrarian land reforms and granted regional autonomy to Catalonia and the Basque Country. Deep ideological polarisation, social unrest and military disaffection culminated in the Spanish Civil War of 1936 to 1939, ending with the defeat of republican forces by General Francisco Franco's nationalists. \n\n Status: Sovereign republic; Capital: Madrid; Official languages: Spanish; Religion: Secular; Government: Unitary semi-presidential republic; Head of state: President; Legislature: Cortes Republicanas; Historical era: Interwar period; Preceded by: Kingdom of Spain; Succeeded by: Spanish State; Currency: Spanish peseta

name: Erik the Red's Land
description: Erik the Red's Land was a contested territory on the uninhabited north-eastern coast of Greenland occupied by Norwegian polar expeditionary personnel on 10 July 1931. Named in honour of the medieval Norse navigator, the territory was administered from the coastal meteorological base of Myggbukta under the authority of governor Helge Ingstad to safeguard Norwegian sealing and whaling interests. Denmark vehemently disputed the occupation before the Permanent Court of International Justice, whose April 1933 ruling in Denmark's favour forced Norway to withdraw its annexation claim. \n\n Status: Unrecognised occupied territory; Administrative seat: Myggbukta; Common languages: Norwegian; Government: Polar colonial administration; Head of state: Monarch of Norway; Ruler title: Governor; Historical era: Interwar period; Preceded by: North Greenland; Succeeded by: North Greenland; Historical region: East Greenland

name: Canada
description: Canada attained full legislative independence from the United Kingdom on 11 December 1931 pursuant to the Statute of Westminster, which recognised the former dominion as an autonomous realm sharing a common monarch. Administered from its federal capital at Ottawa, the vast North American federation exercised absolute authority over its internal and external affairs while navigating the severe economic shocks of the Great Depression. The country mobilised extensive armed forces during the Second World War and subsequently integrated Newfoundland in 1949, consolidating its modern transcontinental boundaries. \n\n Status: Sovereign federation; Capital: Ottawa; Official languages: English and French; Religion: Christianity; Government: Federal parliamentary constitutional monarchy; Ruling dynasty: House of Windsor; Head of state: Monarch; Legislature: Parliament; Currency: Canadian dollar

name: Commonwealth of Australia
description: The Commonwealth of Australia achieved full legislative autonomy within the British Commonwealth on 11 December 1931 under the provisions of the Statute of Westminster. Centred upon the planned national capital of Canberra, the transcontinental federation coordinated national defence and economic policy while six constituent states retained considerable domestic authority. Australia actively prosecuted military operations across the Pacific and European theatres of the Second World War before adopting the Statute formally in 1942, cementing its emergence as an independent Pacific power. \n\n Status: Sovereign federation; Capital: Canberra; Official languages: English; Religion: Christianity; Government: Federal parliamentary constitutional monarchy; Ruling dynasty: House of Windsor; Head of state: Monarch; Legislature: Parliament; Currency: Australian pound

name: Dominion of Newfoundland
description: The Dominion of Newfoundland operated as a self-governing dominion across the island of Newfoundland and the continental coast of Labrador following the passage of the Statute of Westminster on 11 December 1931. Governed by a parliamentary ministry based at St. John's, the territory enjoyed equal constitutional standing with other British dominions but declined to ratify the statute immediately. Confronted by catastrophic public debt and economic paralysis caused by the collapse of the fishing trade, the dominion voluntarily relinquished responsible government in February 1934 to accept direct British commission rule. \n\n Status: British dominion; Capital: St. John's; Official languages: English; Religion: Christianity; Government: Constitutional monarchy under responsible government; Ruling dynasty: House of Windsor; Head of state: Monarch; Legislature: General Assembly; Preceded by: Colony of Newfoundland; Succeeded by: Dominion of Newfoundland; Currency: Newfoundland dollar

name: Union of South Africa
description: The Union of South Africa acquired complete sovereign status on 11 December 1931 under the Statute of Westminster, which eliminated British legislative control over dominion affairs. Comprising the four unified provinces of Cape, Natal, Transvaal and Orange Free State, the state operated with an administrative seat at Pretoria, a legislature at Cape Town and an appellate judiciary at Bloemfontein. Political power was concentrated exclusively among the white minority, whose successive governments enforced discriminatory racial laws that culminated in the formal adoption of apartheid before the union became a republic in 1961. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital: Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein; Official languages: English, Dutch and Afrikaans; Religion: Christianity; Government: Unitary parliamentary constitutional monarchy; Ruling dynasty: House of Windsor; Head of state: Monarch; Legislature: Parliament; Succeeded by: Republic of South Africa; Currency: South African pound

name: Empire of Manchuria
description: The Empire of Manchuria, commonly known as Manchukuo, was a Japanese puppet state established in north-eastern China following the 1931 Kwantung Army invasion of Manchuria. Formally declared in 1932 and elevated to an empire in 1934, the state was administered from Hsinking under the nominal rule of the deposed Qing monarch Puyi. In practice, genuine political and military power resided with the Japanese military apparatus, which exploited Manchuria's extensive agricultural and industrial resources until Soviet forces overran the territory in August 1945. \n\n Status: Puppet state of Imperial Japan; Capital: Hsinking; Common languages: Mandarin Chinese and Japanese; Government: Monarchy under military dictatorship; Head of state: Emperor; Historical era: Interwar and World War II; Preceded by: Republic of China; Succeeded by: Soviet occupation of Manchuria; Currency: Manchukuo yuan

name: Kingdom of Thailand
description: The Kingdom of Thailand, historically known as Siam, was transformed into a constitutional monarchy on 24 June 1932 following a bloodless revolution organised by civilian and military reformers in Bangkok. King Prajadhipok accepted limits on royal prerogative, leading to the creation of a national assembly and modern ministerial governance. Despite frequent military coups and shifting authoritarian administrations, the Southeast Asian kingdom preserved its territorial integrity and cultural traditions, officially adopting the name Thailand in 1939 while navigating external pressure from European empires and Japan. \n\n Status: Sovereign monarchy; Capital: Bangkok; Official languages: Thai; Religion: Theravada Buddhism; Government: Unitary parliamentary constitutional monarchy; Ruling dynasty: Chakri dynasty; Head of state: King; Legislature: National Assembly; Currency: Thai baht

name: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
description: The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia was formally unified on 23 September 1932 when King Abdulaziz ibn Saud issued a royal decree amalgamating the dual kingdoms of Hejaz and Nejd into a single consolidated realm. Ruled from the ancestral oasis citadel of Riyadh, the absolute Islamic monarchy enforced Wahhabi legal tenets across the major holy cities of Mecca and Medina and surrounding desert provinces. The discovery of immense commercial petroleum reserves in 1938 transformed the once impoverished tribal kingdom into a paramount regional and global economic power. \n\n Status: Sovereign monarchy; Capital and largest city: Riyadh; Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Unitary Islamic absolute monarchy; Ruling dynasty: House of Saud; Head of state: King; Historical era: Interwar to present; Preceded by: Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd; Currency: Saudi riyal

name: Kingdom of Iraq
description: The Kingdom of Iraq was recognised as an independent sovereign realm on 3 October 1932 when its British League of Nations mandate terminated and the Hashemite state joined the League as a member. Governed from the historic capital of Baghdad, the kingdom sought to consolidate authority across disparate Sunni, Shia and Kurdish populations while remaining bound to British interests through military base agreements. Internal instability, ethnic tensions and military interventions culminated in an anti-British coup in 1941, though the monarchy was reinstalled and survived until overthrown in 1958. \n\n Status: Sovereign monarchy; Capital: Baghdad; Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Islam; Government: Unitary constitutional monarchy; Ruling dynasty: Hashemite dynasty; Head of state: King; Legislature: Parliament; Historical era: Interwar and World War II; Preceded by: Mandatory Iraq; Currency: Iraqi dinar

name: German Reich
description: The German Reich, known historically as Nazi Germany, was ruled by Adolf Hitler and the National Socialist German Workers' Party following Hitler's appointment as Chancellor on 30 January 1933. Governed from Berlin, the regime abolished the democratic Weimar constitution, dismantled civil liberties and established a brutal totalitarian dictatorship founded upon racial antisemitism and territorial expansionism. The state initiated the Second World War in Europe by invading Poland in September 1939, carrying out the Holocaust and devastating continental warfare until unconditional surrender ended the Reich in May 1945. \n\n Status: Sovereign totalitarian state; Capital: Berlin; Official languages: German; Government: Unitary totalitarian fascist dictatorship; Head of state: Fuhrer and Chancellor; Legislature: Reichstag; Historical era: Interwar and World War II; Preceded by: Weimar Republic; Succeeded by: Allied-occupied Germany; Currency: Reichsmark

name: Republic of Colombia (Military Occupation)
description: The Republic of Colombia military occupation comprised the disputed Amazonian river district surrounding Leticia, which was occupied and fortified by Colombian armed forces between February 1933 and May 1934 during the Colombia-Peru War. Following a surprise seizure of the town by Peruvian irregulars, the Colombian military launched an amphibious expeditionary offensive along the Putumayo and Amazon rivers to reassert national sovereignty. Colombian forces administered the contested border zone until a League of Nations commission supervised the definitive transfer of Leticia back to Colombian civil authority under the Rio de Janeiro Protocol. \n\n Status: Military occupation; Administrative seat: None (military expeditionary command); Official languages: Spanish; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Military occupation administration; Head of state: President of Colombia; Historical era: Interwar period; Preceded by: Republic of Peru; Succeeded by: Republic of Colombia; Historical region: Amazon Basin

name: Portuguese Republic
description: The Portuguese Republic operated under the authoritarian framework of the Estado Novo from 19 March 1933 following the adoption of a new corporatist constitution drafted under Prime Minister Antonio de Oliveira Salazar. Centred upon Lisbon, the regime suppressed political opposition, restricted labour unions and enforced strict social discipline while preserving a vast colonial empire across Africa and Asia. Although Portugal remained officially neutral throughout the Second World War, the regime became embroiled in protracted colonial wars from 1961 until military officers overthrew the dictatorship during the Carnation Revolution of 1974. \n\n Status: Sovereign corporatist republic; Capital: Lisbon; Official languages: Portuguese; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Unitary corporatist one-party republic; Head of state: President; Ruler title: Prime Minister; Legislature: National Assembly; Historical era: Interwar and Cold War; Preceded by: Portuguese Republic; Currency: Portuguese escudo

name: Turkish Islamic Republic of East Turkestan
description: The Turkish Islamic Republic of East Turkestan was a short-lived breakaway state proclaimed on 12 November 1933 amidst the regional Kumul Rebellion against Chinese provincial governance in Xinjiang. Centred in the ancient oasis city of Kashgar, the insurgent administration was led by Uyghur intellectuals and Islamic clerics who enacted a fundamentalist constitution, minted local currency and sought international support for Turkic self-determination. The republic maintained precarious authority across the western Tarim Basin until May 1934, when Chinese Muslim forces loyal to the central government captured Kashgar and dismantled the regime. \n\n Status: Unrecognised Islamic republic; Capital: Kashgar; Official languages: Uyghur; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Islamic republic; Head of state: President; Historical era: Interwar period; Preceded by: Republic of China; Succeeded by: Republic of China; Historical region: East Turkestan

name: Italian Libya
description: Italian Libya was established on 1 January 1934 through the formal administrative amalgamation of the separate Italian colonies of Tripolitania and Cyrenaica alongside the interior military territories of the Sahara. Headquartered in Tripoli, the unified Mediterranean colony was subjected to ambitious infrastructure construction and sponsored mass settlement programmes by Italian colonists under Governor-General Italo Balbo. Following fierce fighting across the North African campaign of the Second World War, Italian colonial rule collapsed when Allied armies captured Tripoli and Benghazi in early 1943, placing the country under British and French military administration. \n\n Status: Colony of Italy; Capital: Tripoli; Common languages: Italian and Arabic; Religion: Islam and Roman Catholicism; Government: Colonial governor-generalship; Ruler title: Governor-General; Head of state: King of Italy; Historical era: Interwar and World War II; Succeeded by: British Military Administration of Libya; Currency: Italian lira

name: Dominion of Newfoundland
description: The Dominion of Newfoundland suspended its representative institutions on 16 February 1934, voluntarily surrendering responsible government in response to acute insolvency brought on by the Great Depression. Administered from St. John's by a six-member Commission of Government appointed by the British Crown and presided over by the colonial governor, the island realm was run without an elected parliament. The direct British trusteeship restructured local finances, modernised fisheries and supervised strategic air and naval bases during the Second World War before voters narrowly approved confederation with Canada in 1949. \n\n Status: British dependency; Capital: St. John's; Official languages: English; Religion: Christianity; Government: Appointed commission of government; Head of state: Monarch of the United Kingdom; Ruler title: Governor; Historical era: Interwar and World War II; Preceded by: Dominion of Newfoundland; Succeeded by: Canada; Currency: Newfoundland dollar

name: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (Military Occupation)
description: The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia military occupation zone comprised the south-western Yemeni border zone and coastal Tihamah, which were occupied by Saudi military detachments in April 1934 during the Saudi-Yemeni War, as well as the later disputed Buraimi Oasis intervention. Under the leadership of Crown Prince Saud and Prince Faisal, Saudi forces rapidly captured the port of Al Hudaydah to enforce peninsular border demarcations against Imam Yahya. The occupation concluded in June 1934 following the signing of the Treaty of Taif, which restored occupied territories to Yemen in exchange for recognised Saudi boundaries. \n\n Status: Military occupation; Administrative seat: None (Saudi expeditionary field command); Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Military occupation administration; Head of state: King of Saudi Arabia; Historical era: Interwar period; Preceded by: Mutawakkilite Kingdom of Yemen; Succeeded by: Mutawakkilite Kingdom of Yemen; Historical region: South Arabia

name: Federal State of Austria
description: The Federal State of Austria was an authoritarian corporatist regime established on 1 May 1934 following the suspension of parliament and the suppression of socialist workers by Chancellor Engelbert Dollfuss. Centred upon Vienna and guided by the Catholic nationalist Fatherland Front, the so-called Standestaat sought to replace liberal democracy with vocational councils influenced by Italian fascism and papal social encyclicals. Beset by severe economic hardship and unrelenting subversion by Austrian National Socialists, the regime collapsed on 12 March 1938 when German Wehrmacht divisions marched in to execute the Anschluss. \n\n Status: Authoritarian corporate state; Capital: Vienna; Official languages: German; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: One-party authoritarian corporate republic; Head of state: President; Ruler title: Chancellor; Historical era: Interwar period; Preceded by: First Austrian Republic; Succeeded by: German Reich; Currency: Austrian schilling

name: Territory of Ashmore and Cartier Islands
description: The Territory of Ashmore and Cartier Islands is an uninhabited external territory of Australia comprising five low-lying tropical islands set within two separate coral reefs in the eastern Timor Sea. Transferred from British imperial jurisdiction to the Commonwealth of Australia on 10 May 1934, the isolated maritime outpost is administered from Canberra under the Australian Department of Infrastructure and Regional Development. The surrounding waters provide traditional harvesting grounds for Indonesian fishermen under bilateral agreements and were designated as national marine nature reserves during the late twentieth century. \n\n Status: External territory of Australia; Administrative seat: None (administered from Canberra); Common languages: English; Government: External territory administration; Head of state: Monarch of Australia; Historical era: Interwar to present; Preceded by: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland; Succeeded by: Commonwealth of Australia; Historical region: Timor Sea

Headquartered in Manila under President Manuel L. Quezon, the administration instituted national defence programmes, adopted Tagalog as a national language and managed autonomous domestic policies while foreign affairs remained under American oversight. name: Spanish State

Operating initially from Burgos and Salamanca under the leadership of General Francisco Franco, the Nationalist authorities unified regular army units, Falangist militias and Carlist requetes into a cohesive fighting force. name: Ireland

Governed from the riverine administrative centre of Rangoon, the colonial administration functioned with a bicameral legislature and a Burmese premier subject to the executive veto of the British governor. Centred upon the historic administrative seat of Antakya, the semi-autonomous polity was jointly supervised by French and Turkish military units following extensive bilateral diplomatic agreements. Ruled as a totalitarian one-party state by Hlinka's Slovak People's Party under Roman Catholic priest Jozef Tiso, the regime aligned closely with Nazi Germany and joined the Axis alliance. Meeting in the regional town of Khust, the local Soim elected nationalist clergyman Avgustyn Voloshyn as president and confirmed Ukrainian as the national language. name: Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia

Administered from Prague Castle by an appointed Reich Protector alongside a pliant Czech puppet cabinet headed by President Emil Hacha, the territory possessed only nominal autonomy. name: Spanish State

Headquartered in Madrid, the nationalist dictatorship banned rival political organisations, centralised regional administrative powers and enforced Catholic moral conservatism through the singular National Movement. name: Kingdom of Albania

Governed from Tirana, the Balkan territory was formally vested in King Victor Emmanuel III, who exercised authority through an Italian lieutenant-general and a collaborative Albanian administration. Centred upon the historic capital of Vilnius, the authoritarian administration of Antanas Smetona struggled to preserve national neutrality while caught between German and Soviet spheres of influence. name: Republic of Estonia

description: The Republic of Estonia experienced the progressive loss of genuine national independence after signing a forced mutual assistance treaty with the Soviet Union in September 1939, permitting the entry of twenty-five thousand Red Army troops. Operating from Tallinn, President Konstantin Pats's authoritarian regime attempted to maintain constitutional continuity while complying with escalating Soviet demands along the Baltic seaboard. In June 1940, Soviet forces blockaded and occupied the country, orchestrated fraudulent parliamentary elections without opposition and coerced the newly appointed puppet legislature into petitioning for integration into the Soviet Union. \n\n Status: Soviet protectorate; Capital: Tallinn; Official languages: Estonian; Religion: Lutheranism and Eastern Orthodoxy; Government: Authoritarian presidential republic; Head of state: President; Historical era: World War II; Preceded by: Republic of Estonia; Succeeded by: Estonian Soviet Socialist Republic; Currency: Estonian kroon

name: Republic of Latvia
label: baltic states
description: The Republic of Latvia was subjected to intense Soviet geopolitical pressure following the signature of the October 1939 mutual assistance treaty, which established extensive Red Army bases along the Courland coastline. Governed from Riga under the personal dictatorship of President Karlis Ulmanis, the Latvian administration attempted to maintain external neutrality while foreign military garrisons circumscribed sovereign domestic authority. The Soviet Union issued an ultimatum in June 1940, invaded the country with massive forces and installed a puppet administration that liquidated Latvian statehood by voting for annexation into the USSR in August. \n\n Status: Soviet protectorate; Capital: Riga; Official languages: Latvian; Religion: Lutheranism, Roman Catholicism and Eastern Orthodoxy; Government: Authoritarian presidential republic; Head of state: President; Historical era: World War II; Preceded by: Republic of Latvia; Succeeded by: Latvian Soviet Socialist Republic; Currency: Latvian lats

name: General Government (Military Occupation)
description: The General Government military occupation was a brutal administrative territory established by Nazi Germany across occupied central Poland following the joint German-Soviet partition of the Second Polish Republic in 1939. Headquartered at the historic Wawel Castle in Krakow under Governor-General Hans Frank, the civilian occupation authorities treated Polish citizens as stateless subjects destined for forced labour and economic exploitation. The territory served as the principal geographic theatre for the Holocaust in Poland, hosting extermination camps such as Treblinka, Belzec, Sobibor and Majdanek before Soviet offensives dismantled the regime in January 1945. \n\n Status: Military civil occupation; Capital: Krakow; Common languages: German and Polish; Religion: Roman Catholicism and Judaism; Government: Colonial civil occupation administration; Ruler title: Governor-General; Historical era: World War II; Preceded by: Second Polish Republic; Succeeded by: Provisional Government of the Republic of Poland; Currency: Zloty and Reichsmark

name: Finnish Democratic Republic

Headquartered in the occupied border resort town of Terijoki under expatriate Finnish communist Otto Wille Kuusinen, the regime claimed legitimate socialist authority over all Finnish territories but received diplomatic recognition exclusively from Moscow. When stubborn Finnish military resistance prevented total Soviet conquest, Joseph Stalin abandoned the Terijoki administration, dissolving the entity upon signing the Moscow Peace Treaty in March 1940. \n\n Status: Soviet puppet government; Administrative seat: Terijoki; Official languages: Finnish and Russian; Government: Provisional communist puppet republic; Head of state: Chairman of the People's Government; Historical era: World War II; Preceded by: Republic of Finland; Succeeded by: Karelo-Finnish Soviet Socialist Republic; Historical region: Karelian Isthmus

name: Kingdom of Denmark
description: The Kingdom of Denmark functioned as a self-governing German protectorate following the rapid Wehrmacht invasion of the Jutland peninsula and Danish islands on 9 April 1940. Administered from Copenhagen, the coalition cabinet under Prime Minister Thorvald Stauning accepted German military occupation in exchange for retaining sovereign domestic autonomy, the royal court under King Christian X and the national parliament. This fragile arrangement endured until escalating Danish civil resistance, sabotage and labour strikes in August 1943 prompted Nazi authorities to impose direct martial law and dissolve the Danish armed forces. \n\n Status: German protectorate; Capital: Copenhagen; Official languages: Danish; Religion: Lutheranism; Government: Constitutional monarchy under occupation; Head of state: King of Denmark; Ruler title: Prime Minister; Legislature: Folketing; Historical era: World War II; Succeeded by: German military administration in Denmark; Currency: Danish krone

Operating without a central civilian capital, joint Allied expeditionary forces governed transitional operational zones across western Norway, southern Italy, western Germany and strategic transatlantic supply routes. Allied military authorities coordinated logistics, restored civilian public utilities and maintained territorial security until sovereign national governments were re-established or formal four-power occupation zones were inaugurated following Axis capitulation. \n\n Status: Joint military occupation; Administrative seat: None (Allied joint military command); Common languages: English and French; Government: Joint military administration; Ruler title: Supreme Allied Commander; Historical era: World War II; Preceded by: Axis Powers; Succeeded by: Allied-occupied Germany

name: Colony of Martinique

Administered from Fort-de-France, the Caribbean island colony became isolated by a strict United States naval blockade that immobilised several French warships and vast reserves of national gold bullion stored on the island. The local population suffered acute shortages of food and medical supplies until popular unrest and military insubordination compelled Robert to surrender administration to Free French authorities in July 1943. \n\n Status: French colony loyal to Vichy; Capital: Fort-de-France; Official languages: French; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Colonial naval administration; Ruler title: High Commissioner of the French Antilles; Historical era: World War II; Preceded by: French Third Republic; Succeeded by: Free France; Currency: French franc

Administered from the port settlement of Gustavia, the small Leeward island experienced severe economic hardship and trade disruption caused by Allied naval patrols monitoring Vichy-held territories in the West Indies. Local officials maintained nominal loyalty to Marshal Philippe Petain's government until political sentiment shifted across the French Antilles in July 1943, enabling Free French representatives to assume administrative control without armed conflict. \n\n Status: French dependency loyal to Vichy; Administrative seat: Gustavia; Official languages: French; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Island colonial administration; Head of state: Head of the French State; Ruler title: Governor of Guadeloupe; Historical era: World War II; Preceded by: French Third Republic; Succeeded by: Free France; Currency: French franc

name: Colony of Saint-Martin
description: The Colony of Saint-Martin encompassed the northern French sector of the divided Caribbean island, remaining under the authority of the Vichy regime following the collapse of the French Third Republic in June 1940. Governed locally from the coastal town of Marigot as a dependency of Guadeloupe, the island faced severe commercial isolation alongside its Dutch southern neighbour due to British and American maritime controls. Vichy oversight ended peacefully in mid-July 1943 when the local administration aligned itself with the French Committee of National Liberation. \n\n Status: French dependency loyal to Vichy; Administrative seat: Marigot; Official languages: French; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Colonial dependency administration; Head of state: Head of the French State; Ruler title: Governor of Guadeloupe; Historical era: World War II; Preceded by: French Third Republic; Succeeded by: Free France; Currency: French franc

name: Colony of the Wallis and Futuna Islands
description: The Colony of the Wallis and Futuna Islands adhered to the Petainist Vichy government following the 1940 armistice, governed locally from Mata-Utu by a French colonial resident in conjunction with traditional indigenous kings. Isolated across the South Pacific, the remote archipelago maintained its conservative Catholic and pro-Vichy alignment even as neighbouring French Pacific territories rallied to General Charles de Gaulle. The colony's allegiance came to an abrupt end on 27 May 1942 when Free French naval forces aboard the armed merchant cruiser Chevreuil staged a bloodless amphibious landing, deposing the Vichy resident. \n\n Status: French protectorate loyal to Vichy; Capital: Mata-Utu; Official languages: French; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Colonial residency under customary monarchy; Ruler title: Colonial Resident; Head of state: Head of the French State; Historical era: World War II; Preceded by: French Third Republic; Succeeded by: Free France; Currency: CFP franc

name: French Establishments in India

Following the June 1940 armistice between France and Nazi Germany, Governor Horace Crocicchia initially declared allegiance to Marshal Petain's government in Vichy. However, encircled entirely by British India and pressured by intense local merchant sentiment, the colonial assembly conducted a popular consultation in September 1940 that overwhelmingly endorsed Free France, making the Indian comptoirs among the earliest colonies to rally to Charles de Gaulle. \n\n Status: French colony loyal to Vichy; Capital: Pondicherry; Official languages: French; Common languages: Tamil, Bengali, Malayalam and Telugu; Religion: Hinduism, Roman Catholicism and Islam; Government: Colonial governor-generalship; Ruler title: Governor; Historical era: World War II; Preceded by: French Third Republic; Succeeded by: Free France; Currency: French Indian rupee

name: French Establishments in Oceania
description: The French Establishments in Oceania encompassed five extensive archipelagos across eastern Polynesia, administered from the colonial port of Papeete on the island of Tahiti. Following the fall of France in June 1940, Governor Jean Chastenet de Gery initially maintained allegiance to the collaborationist Vichy regime, prompting widespread anxiety among British and Commonwealth neighbours in the Pacific. Frustrated by economic isolation and strong Gaullist sympathies, local French and Tahitian residents organised a consultative plebiscite on 2 September 1940, peacefully removing the Vichy administration and pledging the islands to Free France. \n\n Status: French colony loyal to Vichy; Capital: Papeete; Official languages: French and Tahitian; Religion: Protestantism and Roman Catholicism; Government: Colonial administration; Ruler title: Governor; Head of state: Head of the French State; Historical era: World War II; Preceded by: French Third Republic; Succeeded by: Free France; Currency: CFP franc

name: French Guiana

The equatorial South American territory, known internationally for its penal colony at Devil's Island, suffered economic strangulation caused by Allied maritime surveillance along the Atlantic seaboard. Mounting domestic disaffection and friction among colonial garrison officers culminated in a bloodless civilian and military demonstration in March 1943 that ousted the Vichy governor and declared allegiance to Free France. \n\n Status: French colony loyal to Vichy; Capital: Cayenne; Official languages: French; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Colonial governor-generalship; Ruler title: Governor; Head of state: Head of the French State; Historical era: World War II; Preceded by: French Third Republic; Succeeded by: Free France; Currency: French franc

name: French State
description: The French State, commonly designated as Vichy France, was established in July 1940 following France's catastrophic military collapse against Nazi Germany and the vote of the National Assembly granting constituent powers to Marshal Philippe Petain. Headquartered in the spa resort town of Vichy, the authoritarian regime exercised nominal authority over metropolitan France and the colonial empire while Germany directly occupied the northern and Atlantic zones. Petain replaced the republican motto with National Revolution doctrines until Allied landings in North Africa provoked the total German military occupation of southern France in November 1942. \n\n Status: German client state; Capital: Vichy; Official languages: French; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Unitary authoritarian dictatorship; Head of state: Head of the French State; Ruler title: Prime Minister; Historical era: World War II; Preceded by: French Third Republic; Succeeded by: German military administration in France; Currency: French franc

name: Guadeloupe
description: Guadeloupe functioned under the authoritarian jurisdiction of the Vichy regime following the June 1940 armistice, governed locally from Basse-Terre by colonial administrators subordinated to Admiral Georges Robert in Martinique. The Caribbean archipelago suffered severe economic isolation as the Allied blockade severed trade routes, preventing sugar exports and causing widespread shortages of flour, fuel and clothing. Popular dissent expanded rapidly among the Afro-Caribbean populace, culminating in July 1943 when local military units joined civilian demonstrations to overthrow Vichy authority and transfer governance to the French Committee of National Liberation. \n\n Status: French colony loyal to Vichy; Capital: Basse-Terre; Official languages: French; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Colonial administration; Ruler title: Governor; Head of state: Head of the French State; Historical era: World War II; Preceded by: French Third Republic; Succeeded by: Free France; Currency: French franc

name: Colony of Chad
description: The Colony of Chad experienced a fleeting period of nominal allegiance to the Vichy French government during the weeks following the capitulation of the French Third Republic in July 1940. Centred administratively upon Fort-Lamy, the vast Saharan territory was governed by Felix Eboue, an astute colonial administrator of French Guianese origin. Recognising the impossibility of defending the colony under Axis patronage, Eboue covertly coordinated with General Charles de Gaulle and boldly proclaimed Chad's accession to Free France on 26 August 1940, securing a crucial strategic springboard for Allied operations. \n\n Status: French colony loyal to Vichy; Capital: Fort-Lamy; Official languages: French; Religion: Islam, Christianity and traditional beliefs; Government: Colonial governor-generalship; Ruler title: Governor; Head of state: Head of the French State; Historical era: World War II; Preceded by: French Third Republic; Succeeded by: Free France; Currency: French Equatorial African franc

name: Colony of Madagascar and Dependencies
description: The Colony of Madagascar and Dependencies remained loyal to the Vichy regime following the defeat of France, governed from the highland capital of Antananarivo by Governor-General Armand Annet. The Indian Ocean island held profound maritime importance along Allied merchant shipping lanes around the Cape of Good Hope, prompting British apprehensions that Vichy authorities might concede naval bases to Imperial Japan. In May 1942, British forces launched Operation Ironclad, an amphibious assault that subdued fierce Vichy resistance across the island and culminated in Annet's formal surrender to Allied commanders in November 1942. \n\n Status: French colony loyal to Vichy; Capital: Antananarivo; Common languages: French and Malagasy; Religion: Christianity, traditional beliefs and Islam; Government: Colonial governor-generalship; Ruler title: Governor-General; Head of state: Head of the French State; Historical era: World War II; Preceded by: French Third Republic; Succeeded by: Free France; Currency: Malagasy franc

name: Colony of Réunion
description: The Colony of Reunion maintained allegiance to the collaborationist Vichy government following the 1940 armistice, governed from Saint-Denis by Governor Pierre Aubert. Positioned in the western Indian Ocean, the island colony endured maritime isolation and severe food shortages due to Allied naval surveillance. Vichy control persisted until 28 November 1942, when the Free French destroyer Leopard arrived off Saint-Denis and landed troops, sparking a brief artillery skirmish that persuaded Aubert to surrender the administration to Free French authorities two days later. \n\n Status: French colony loyal to Vichy; Capital: Saint-Denis; Official languages: French; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Colonial administration; Ruler title: Governor; Head of state: Head of the French State; Historical era: World War II; Preceded by: French Third Republic; Succeeded by: Free France; Currency: French franc

name: Colony of Saint-Pierre and Miquelon
description: The Colony of Saint-Pierre and Miquelon was an isolated archipelago situated off the southern coast of Newfoundland that adhered to the Vichy French regime under Governor Gilbert de Bournat. The presence of a Vichy-controlled maritime outpost possessing a powerful wireless radio station adjacent to transatlantic shipping lanes alarmed Canadian and American authorities. On 24 December 1941, Free French naval vessels under Admiral Emile Muselier executed a surprise, bloodless landing on Saint-Pierre, dissolving the Vichy administration and holding a plebiscite in which islanders overwhelmingly affirmed loyalty to Free France. \n\n Status: French colony loyal to Vichy; Capital: Saint-Pierre; Official languages: French; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Colonial administration; Ruler title: Governor; Head of state: Head of the French State; Historical era: World War II; Preceded by: French Third Republic; Succeeded by: Free France; Currency: French franc

name: Colony of Ubangi-Shari
description: The Colony of Ubangi-Shari maintained a brief and unsettled allegiance to the Vichy regime following the establishment of Marshal Petain's government in July 1940. Governed from Bangui on the Ubangi River, the central African territory was caught between competing factions of colonial officials debating whether to accept the metropolitan armistice or join Charles de Gaulle's resistance movement. Inspired by the decisive action of neighbouring Chad under Felix Eboue, local military officers and civil servants staged a bloodless coup on 26 August 1940, aligning Ubangi-Shari definitively with Free France. \n\n Status: French colony loyal to Vichy; Capital: Bangui; Official languages: French; Religion: Traditional beliefs, Christianity and Islam; Government: Colonial governor-generalship; Ruler title: Governor; Head of state: Head of the French State; Historical era: World War II; Preceded by: French Third Republic; Succeeded by: Free France; Currency: French Equatorial African franc

name: French Algeria
description: French Algeria remained under the strict authority of the collaborationist Vichy regime between July 1940 and November 1942, administered from Algiers as three integrated overseas departments of France. The authoritarian colonial government repealed the Cremieux Decree, stripping Algerian Jews of French citizenship, and enforced harsh surveillance over both European settlers and the disenfranchised Muslim majority. Vichy hegemony ended dramatically on 8 November 1942 when Anglo-American forces landed in North Africa during Operation Torch, prompting local French garrisons to defect to the Allied cause after brief resistance. \n\n Status: French territory loyal to Vichy; Capital: Algiers; Official languages: French; Common languages: Algerian Arabic and Berber; Religion: Islam, Roman Catholicism and Judaism; Government: Colonial governor-generalship; Ruler title: Governor-General; Head of state: Head of the French State; Historical era: World War II; Succeeded by: Free France; Currency: Algerian franc

name: French Cameroon
description: French Cameroon was a League of Nations mandate in Central Africa that briefly adhered to the Vichy regime following the military armistice of June 1940. Headquartered in Yaounde, the colonial administration faced immediate internal ideological division between conservative officials loyal to Marshal Petain and younger officers determined to continue the anti-German war effort. On 27 August 1940, Free French emissary Philippe Leclerc landed at Douala with a small force, successfully rallying local soldiers and civil servants to depose the Vichy governor without bloodshed within twenty-four hours. \n\n Status: French mandate loyal to Vichy; Capital: Yaounde; Official languages: French; Religion: Christianity, traditional beliefs and Islam; Government: Mandatory governor-generalship; Ruler title: Commissioner; Head of state: Head of the French State; Historical era: World War II; Preceded by: French Third Republic; Succeeded by: Free France; Currency: French franc

name: French Congo
description: The French Congo, then known administratively as Middle Congo within French Equatorial Africa, briefly adhered to the Vichy government following France's defeat in July 1940. Centred upon Brazzaville on the Congo River, the colony witnessed acute political friction between senior colonial administrators loyal to Petain and anti-fascist military officers. Coordinated closely with neighbouring uprisings in Chad and Cameroon, Gaullist sympathisers led by Colonel Edgard de Larminat seized key administrative buildings in Brazzaville on 26 August 1940, transforming the city into the spiritual and military capital of Free France. \n\n Status: French colony loyal to Vichy; Capital: Brazzaville; Official languages: French; Religion: Christianity and traditional beliefs; Government: Colonial administration; Ruler title: Lieutenant-Governor; Head of state: Head of the French State; Historical era: World War II; Preceded by: French Third Republic; Succeeded by: Free France; Currency: French Equatorial African franc

name: French Protectorate in Morocco
description: The French Protectorate in Morocco was governed under the supervision of the Vichy regime following the Franco-German armistice, administered from Rabat by Resident-General Auguste Nogues in nominal coordination with Sultan Mohammed V. The colonial administration introduced anti-Jewish legislation and enforced strict economic rationing, although the Sultan subtly protected Jewish subjects from the most severe persecution. Administered from the town of Uzice under Josip Broz Tito and the Supreme Staff, the revolutionary administration established people's liberation committees, published newspapers, operated an arms factory and maintained defensive lines. Administered from Sabha by French military governors and indigenous notables of the Sayf an-Nasr family, the zone was managed separately from British-controlled Tripolitania and Cyrenaica. name: British Military Administration of Libya

Administered primarily from Tripoli under a British chief administrator, the military authority maintained civil stability, repaired war-damaged harbour infrastructure and supervised local municipal governance under the provisions of the Hague Conventions. Governed from Rangoon under Ba Maw, who held the title of Head of State, the regime proclaimed national independence, adopted Burmese as its primary official tongue and established the Burma National Army. Situated across two principal mountainous landmasses and numerous smaller islands in the southwestern Pacific Ocean, the parliamentary democracy preserved the British monarch as its ceremonial head of state while developing independent external relations. Centred in the coastal commercial hub of Colombo, the island nation was governed through a Westminster-style parliamentary framework initially led by Prime Minister D. S. Senanayake. Based institutionally in Jerusalem and Tel Aviv, the parliamentary republic absorbed hundreds of thousands of Jewish refugees from post-war Europe and the wider Middle East while developing advanced agricultural, scientific and military capabilities. Operating primarily across the Galilee and northern hills of Palestine, the multi-national force sought to resist Zionist territorial expansion and defend Arab communities without placing units under the command of Transjordan. These occupational administrations proved ephemeral, terminating either through negotiated transfers to allied armies as in 1949 or via decisive multinational military intervention as during the Gulf War. \n\n Status: Military occupation administration; Capital: None (decentralised); Administrative seat: Baghdad; Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Islam; Government: Military command administration; Ruler title: Commander-in-Chief; Historical era: Cold War to Gulf War; Established: 24 May 1948; Currency: Iraqi dinar

name: Syria (Military Occupation)
description: Syria under Military Occupation designates foreign territories garrisoned and controlled by the Syrian Armed Forces, most prominently its prolonged military deployment across Lebanon between 1976 and 2005. Deployed originally under an Arab League peacekeeping mandate during the Lebanese Civil War, Syrian intelligence agencies and military garrisons maintained decisive political and security dominance throughout the country. name: Lebanese Republic (Military Occupation)
description: The Lebanese Republic under Military Occupation comprised limited forward positions in northern Palestine occupied by the Lebanese Armed Forces during the 1948 Arab-Israeli War. Operating across the upper Galilee border zone, Lebanese troops established defensive security outposts and supported local Arab militias against advancing Israeli brigades. Lebanese military authority in these tactical border pockets ceased with the signing of the formal Israel-Lebanon Armistice Agreement at Ras al-Naqoura in March 1949, which restored the international frontier. \n\n Status: Military occupation administration; Capital: Beirut; Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Christianity and Islam; Government: Military field administration; Ruler title: Commander of the Armed Forces; Historical era: 1948 Arab-Israeli War; Established: 6 June 1948; Disestablished: 20 July 1949; Preceded by: Mandatory Palestine; Succeeded by: State of Israel; Currency: Lebanese pound

name: Republic of Korea
description: The Republic of Korea was formally inaugurated on 15 August 1948 across the southern half of the Korean Peninsula following United Nations-supervised elections. Governed from Seoul under its founding president Syngman Rhee, the young state repelled northern communist aggression during the devastating Korean War with substantial United Nations assistance. Over subsequent decades, South Korea transitioned from an agrarian economy under authoritarian governance into a vibrant high-technology democracy and one of East Asia's leading industrial powers. \n\n Status: Sovereign presidential republic; Capital: Seoul; Official languages: Korean; Religion: Christianity, Buddhism and irreligion; Government: Unitary presidential constitutional republic; Ruler title: President; Head of state: Syngman Rhee; Legislature: National Assembly; Historical era: Cold War to contemporary; Established: 15 August 1948; Preceded by: United States Army Military Government in Korea; Currency: South Korean won

name: Democratic People's Republic of Korea
description: The Democratic People's Republic of Korea was established on 9 September 1948 across the northern portion of the Korean Peninsula under the leadership of Kim Il Sung. Governed from Pyongyang as a centralised socialist state, the regime initiated the Korean War in June 1950 in an unsuccessful attempt to reunify the peninsula under communist control. Following the 1953 armistice, the state developed the idiosyncratic ideology of Juche, prioritising intense militarisation, economic autarky and hereditary dynastic governance under the Workers' Party of Korea. \n\n Status: Sovereign socialist state; Capital: Pyongyang; Official languages: Korean; Religion: State atheism and Juche; Government: Unitary one-party socialist republic; Ruler title: Supreme Leader; Head of state: Kim Il Sung; Legislature: Supreme People's Assembly; Historical era: Cold War to contemporary; Established: 9 September 1948; Preceded by: People's Committee of North Korea; Currency: North Korean won

name: State of Israel (Military Occupation)
description: Israel under Military Occupation represents territories brought under the operational control of the Israel Defence Forces beyond the state's recognised borders, notably the West Bank, the Gaza Strip, the Sinai Peninsula and southern Lebanon. Instituted through military governorates following successive Arab-Israeli wars, these administrative commands supervised civilian infrastructure, security checkpoints and resource distribution. While direct occupation in Sinai and southern Lebanon terminated through treaty withdrawals, military control over key Palestinian territories persisted across subsequent decades. \n\n Status: Military occupation administration; Capital: None (decentralised); Administrative seat: Tel Aviv; Common languages: Hebrew and Arabic; Religion: Judaism and Islam; Government: Military governorate; Ruler title: Minister of Defence; Historical era: Cold War to contemporary; Established: 30 December 1948; Currency: Israeli pound and Israeli new shekel

name: Emirate of Cyrenaica
description: The Emirate of Cyrenaica was an independent Senussi state proclaimed in eastern Libya on 1 March 1949 by Sayyid Idris with British diplomatic backing. Governed from Benghazi, the emirate re-established traditional Senussi political authority, adopted a national flag and organised basic civil ministries while British advisers oversaw foreign relations. The autonomous emirate was superseded on 24 December 1951 when Idris was enthroned as monarch of the newly unified Kingdom of Libya, integrating Cyrenaica with Tripolitania and Fezzan. \n\n Status: Sovereign monarchy; Capital: Benghazi; Common languages: Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Absolute monarchy; Ruler title: Emir; Head of state: Idris; Historical era: Post-war era; Established: 1 March 1949; Disestablished: 24 December 1951; Preceded by: British Military Administration in Cyrenaica; Succeeded by: Kingdom of Libya; Currency: Egyptian pound

name: Federal Republic of Germany
description: The Federal Republic of Germany was established on 23 May 1949 through the promulgation of the Basic Law across the American, British and French occupation zones. Administered from its provisional capital at Bonn, the democratic federation enacted a social market economy, integrated rapidly into Western defence structures through NATO, and served as an engine of European integration. Following the peaceful collapse of the communist regime in East Germany, the country achieved national reunification on 3 October 1990 and restored Berlin as the federal capital. \n\n Status: Sovereign federal parliamentary republic; Capital: Bonn; Official languages: German; Religion: Roman Catholicism, Protestantism and secularism; Government: Federal parliamentary republic; Ruler title: Federal Chancellor; Head of state: Theodor Heuss; Legislature: Bundestag and Bundesrat; Historical era: Cold War to contemporary; Established: 23 May 1949; Preceded by: Allied-occupied Germany; Currency: Deutsche Mark

name: State of Vietnam
description: The State of Vietnam was established on 2 July 1949 as an associated state within the French Union under the leadership of former emperor Bao Dai. Formed through the Elysee Accords as an anti-communist nationalist alternative to the Viet Minh, the state exercised internal administrative authority over major urban centres while France retained control over defence and foreign policy. The regime participated alongside French expeditionary forces in the First Indochina War until the Geneva Accords of July 1954 partitioned Vietnam along the seventeenth parallel. \n\n Status: Associated state of the French Union; Capital: Saigon; Official languages: Vietnamese and French; Religion: Buddhism, Confucianism, Catholicism and Caodaism; Government: Constitutional monarchy within the French Union; Ruler title: Chief of State; Head of state: Bao Dai; Historical era: First Indochina War; Established: 2 July 1949; Disestablished: 21 July 1954; Preceded by: French Indochina; Succeeded by: State of Vietnam; Currency: French Indochinese piastre

name: Hungarian People's Republic

description: The Hungarian People's Republic was formally proclaimed on 20 August 1949 with the adoption of a Soviet-style socialist constitution. Based in Budapest and led by the Hungarian Working People's Party under Matyas Rakosi, the regime enforced Stalinist industrialisation and ideological repression that provoked the nationwide Hungarian Revolution of 1956. Following the Soviet military suppression of the uprising, the government under Janos Kadar developed a pragmatic model termed Goulash Communism before negotiating a peaceful transition to democracy in October 1989. \n\n Status: Sovereign socialist republic; Capital: Budapest; Official languages: Hungarian; Religion: State atheism; Government: Unitary Marxist-Leninist one-party republic; Ruler title: General Secretary; Head of state: Matyas Rakosi; Legislature: National Assembly; Historical era: Cold War; Established: 20 August 1949; Disestablished: 23 October 1989; Preceded by: Republic of Hungary; Succeeded by: Republic of Hungary; Currency: Hungarian forint

name: People's Republic of China
description: The People's Republic of China was proclaimed on 1 October 1949 by Mao Zedong in Beijing following the victory of the Chinese Communist Party in the Chinese Civil War. The revolutionary state transformed agrarian society through extensive land redistribution, collectivisation and heavy industrial programs while consolidating control over Tibet and Xinjiang. Following Mao's death, comprehensive economic reforms initiated under Deng Xiaoping in 1978 propelled China into a global industrial powerhouse while retaining strict one-party socialist governance. \n\n Status: Sovereign socialist state; Capital: Beijing; Official languages: Standard Chinese; Religion: State atheism; Government: Unitary Marxist-Leninist one-party socialist republic; Ruler title: Chairman of the Chinese Communist Party; Head of state: Mao Zedong; Legislature: National People's Congress; Historical era: Cold War to contemporary; Established: 1 October 1949; Preceded by: Republic of China; Currency: Renminbi

name: German Democratic Republic

description: The German Democratic Republic was founded on 7 October 1949 in the Soviet occupation zone of post-war Germany, establishing its capital in East Berlin. Governed monopolistically by the Socialist Unity Party under Walter Ulbricht and later Erich Honecker, the state built the Berlin Wall in 1961 to halt outward emigration and maintained extensive domestic surveillance through the Stasi. A founding member of the Warsaw Pact, East Germany functioned as Moscow's westernmost European bastion until mass peaceful demonstrations precipitated its reunification with West Germany on 3 October 1990. \n\n Status: Sovereign socialist state; Capital: East Berlin; Official languages: German; Religion: State atheism; Government: Unitary Marxist-Leninist one-party republic; Ruler title: General Secretary; Head of state: Wilhelm Pieck; Legislature: Volkskammer; Historical era: Cold War; Established: 7 October 1949; Disestablished: 3 October 1990; Preceded by: Soviet occupation zone in Germany; Succeeded by: Federal Republic of Germany; Currency: East German mark

name: Republic of China
description: The Republic of China relocated its central seat of government to Taipei on 7 December 1949 following the loss of the Chinese mainland to communist armies in the Chinese Civil War. Exercising jurisdiction over Taiwan, Penghu, Kinmen and Matsu, the nationalist government under Chiang Kai-shek initially enforced martial law while engineering rapid export-led industrialisation. Taiwan democratised during the late twentieth century, lifting martial law in 1987 and establishing a multiparty constitutional democracy with a globally competitive semiconductor manufacturing economy. \n\n Status: Sovereign republic; Capital: Taipei; Official languages: Standard Chinese; Religion: Buddhism, Taoism and Christianity; Government: Unitary semi-presidential republic; Ruler title: President; Head of state: Chiang Kai-shek; Legislature: Legislative Yuan; Historical era: Cold War to contemporary; Established: 7 December 1949; Preceded by: Republic of China; Currency: New Taiwan dollar

name: Netherlands New Guinea
description: Netherlands New Guinea was a Dutch colonial territory encompassing the western half of the island of New Guinea that was retained by the Kingdom of the Netherlands after Indonesia gained independence in December 1949. Administered from Hollandia, Dutch officials sought to prepare the indigenous Papuan population for eventual self-determination, introducing a legislative New Guinea Council and adopting national emblems in 1961.
