The territory completed detailed constitutional negotiations, achieving full sovereign independence as a two-island federal realm in September 1983. \n\n Status: Associated state of the United Kingdom; Capital: Basseterre; Official languages: English; Government: Constitutional monarchy under associated statehood; Head of state: Elizabeth II; Legislature: House of Assembly; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 19 December 1980; Disestablished: 19 September 1983; Preceded by: Saint Christopher-Nevis-Anguilla; Succeeded by: Federation of Saint Kitts and Nevis; Currency: East Caribbean dollar

name: Tswanaland
label: bantustans
description: Tswanaland was created in 1981 in eastern South West Africa near the border with Botswana, serving as a segregated homeland for the territory's Batswana community. Centred at Aminuis, the homeland possessed an appointed second-tier ethnic representative council that handled limited communal matters under South African apartheid oversight. The small and economically isolated entity possessed no true political sovereignty and was liquidated in June 1989 to facilitate the unified independence of Namibia. \n\n Status: Bantustan and ethnic representative authority; Capital: Aminuis; Common languages: Setswana, Afrikaans and English; Government: Apartheid tribal authority; Historical era: Late Cold War; Established: 1981; Disestablished: 1 June 1989; Preceded by: South West Africa; Succeeded by: Republic of Namibia; Currency: South African rand

name: KwaNdebele
label: bantustans
description: KwaNdebele was established on 1 April 1981 as a self-governing bantustan in South Africa's central Transvaal, designated as the national homeland for the Ndebele people. Headquartered at KwaMhlanga, the homeland was formed by assembling scattered tracts of farmland, sparking intense local resistance when officials attempted to impose nominal independence. The fragmented territory endured major popular rebellions until it was permanently abolished and absorbed into South Africa during the democratic transition of April 1994. \n\n Status: Self-governing bantustan; Capital: KwaMhlanga; Common languages: Southern Ndebele, Northern Ndebele and Afrikaans; Government: Subnational parliamentary tribal authority; Historical era: Late Cold War; Established: 1 April 1981; Disestablished: 27 April 1994; Preceded by: Republic of South Africa; Succeeded by: Republic of South Africa; Currency: South African rand

name: Belize
description: Belize attained sovereign statehood on 21 September 1981, bringing an end to more than a century of British colonial administration over British Honduras. Governed from the purpose-built inland capital of Belmopan, the Central American nation established a stable parliamentary democracy and retained the British monarch as head of state. Despite historical territorial disputes with neighbouring Guatemala, the country preserved its territorial boundaries while cultivating maritime tourism and agricultural commerce. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital: Belmopan; Largest city: Belize City; Official languages: English; Common languages: Belizean Creole and Spanish; Government: Unitary parliamentary constitutional monarchy; Head of state: Elizabeth II; Legislature: National Assembly; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 21 September 1981; Preceded by: British Honduras; Currency: Belize dollar

name: Antigua and Barbuda
description: Antigua and Barbuda gained full independence on 1 November 1981 as a sovereign constitutional monarchy and Commonwealth realm in the eastern Caribbean. Centred at St. John's on Antigua, the nation encompasses the sister island of Barbuda along with several smaller uninhabited islets. The state established an enduring parliamentary system, transforming its historical sugar economy into a thriving commercial hub focused on luxury maritime tourism and international financial services. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: St. John's; Official languages: English; Government: Unitary parliamentary constitutional monarchy; Head of state: Elizabeth II; Legislature: Parliament; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 1 November 1981; Preceded by: Antigua; Currency: East Caribbean dollar

name: Senegambia Confederation
description: The Senegambia Confederation was instituted on 1 February 1982 through an agreement uniting Senegal and The Gambia following a Senegalese military intervention that protected the Gambian government. Coordinated between Dakar and Banjul, the confederation sought to integrate armed forces, coordinate regional diplomacy, and foster shared economic policies while preserving each nation's independent statehood. Persistent differences over commercial tariffs and Gambian fears of domination led Senegal to unilaterally terminate the confederation in September 1989. \n\n Status: Confederation of sovereign states; Capital: Dakar and Banjul; Official languages: French and English; Common languages: Wolof and Mandinka; Government: Confederal presidency; Ruler title: President; First ruler: Abdou Diouf; Historical era: Cold War; Established: 1 February 1982; Disestablished: 30 September 1989; Preceded by: Republic of Senegal and Republic of The Gambia; Succeeded by: Republic of Senegal and Republic of The Gambia; Currency: West African CFA franc and Gambian dalasi

name: Islamic Republic of Iran (Military Occupation)
description: The Islamic Republic of Iran (Military Occupation) comprised the forward operational salients held by Iranian military units and revolutionary guards inside Iraqi territory during the Iran-Iraq War. Following the liberation of its own invaded soil in 1982, Iran launched counter-offensives across the frontier, capturing strategic positions including the oil-producing Fao Peninsula and areas surrounding Basra. Governed through military commanders in the field without a fixed capital, these captured enclaves were held until Iraqi forces recaptured them prior to the 1988 ceasefire. \n\n Status: Military occupation; Administrative seat: Military field command; Official languages: Persian; Religion: Twelver Shia Islam; Government: Military administration; Historical era: Cold War; Established: 16 July 1982; Disestablished: 1 November 1988; Preceded by: Republic of Iraq; Succeeded by: Republic of Iraq; Currency: Iranian rial

name: Federation of Saint Christopher and Nevis
description: The Federation of Saint Christopher and Nevis gained full sovereign independence on 19 September 1983, becoming the smallest sovereign federal state in the Western Hemisphere. Headquartered at Basseterre on Saint Kitts, the constitutional monarchy guarantees statutory local autonomy to the island of Nevis under a shared federal parliament. The country transitioned from state-run sugarcane farming into an upscale service-driven economy sustained by luxury tourism, offshore banking, and citizenship investment. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Basseterre; Official languages: English; Government: Federal parliamentary constitutional monarchy; Head of state: Elizabeth II; Legislature: National Assembly; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 19 September 1983; Preceded by: Saint Christopher and Nevis; Currency: East Caribbean dollar

name: Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus
description: The Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus was proclaimed on 15 November 1983, formalising an autonomous Turkish Cypriot state across the northern third of the island of Cyprus. Headquartered at North Nicosia, the self-declared republic remains recognised internationally solely by Turkey, which maintains military forces and provides substantial financial support. The state operates a semi-presidential democracy separated from the southern Republic of Cyprus by a United Nations-supervised buffer zone. \n\n Status: Partially recognised sovereign state; Capital and largest city: North Nicosia; Official languages: Turkish; Common languages: Cypriot Turkish; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Unitary semi-presidential republic; Legislature: Assembly of the Republic; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 15 November 1983; Preceded by: Turkish Federated State of Cyprus; Currency: Turkish lira

name: Brunei Darussalam
description: Brunei Darussalam regained complete sovereign independence on 1 January 1984, ending nearly a century of British protectorate administration over the coastal Borneo sultanate. Governed from Bandar Seri Begawan by Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah as an absolute Islamic monarchy, the nation deployed its abundant offshore petroleum and gas wealth to finance an extensive welfare system. The sultanate maintained political harmony under its official Malay Islamic Monarchy doctrine, playing an active diplomatic role in ASEAN affairs. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Bandar Seri Begawan; Official languages: Malay; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Unitary Islamic absolute monarchy; Ruler title: Sultan; First ruler: Hassanal Bolkiah; Legislature: Legislative Council; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 1 January 1984; Preceded by: State of Brunei; Currency: Brunei dollar

name: Burkina Faso
description: Burkina Faso was adopted as the official sovereign name of the former Upper Volta on 4 August 1984 under the revolutionary presidency of Thomas Sankara. Governed from Ouagadougou, the landlocked West African state pursued sweeping socio-economic reforms including nationwide tree planting, mass vaccinations, and agrarian self-reliance. Following Sankara's assassination in 1987, the nation underwent political reorganisation while remaining an active agricultural producer in the Sahel. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Ouagadougou; Official languages: French; Common languages: Moore, Dyula and Fula; Government: Unitary republic; Legislature: National Assembly; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 4 August 1984; Preceded by: Republic of Upper Volta; Currency: West African CFA franc

name: KaNgwane
label: bantustans
description: KaNgwane was granted nominal self-governing status on 31 August 1984 as an apartheid homeland in eastern Transvaal, designated for the Swazi population of South Africa. Centred at Louieville, the territory had resisted previous attempts by Pretoria to cede its lands to neighbouring Swaziland in 1982. Led by Chief Minister Enos Mabuza, the local government rejected complete nominal independence and worked alongside anti-apartheid groups until reincorporation into South Africa in April 1994. \n\n Status: Self-governing bantustan; Capital: Louieville; Common languages: Swazi, English and Afrikaans; Government: Subnational parliamentary tribal authority; Head of state: Enos Mabuza; Historical era: Late Cold War; Established: 31 August 1984; Disestablished: 27 April 1994; Preceded by: Republic of South Africa; Succeeded by: Republic of South Africa; Currency: South African rand

name: Territorial Collectivity of Saint-Pierre and Miquelon
description: The Territorial Collectivity of Saint-Pierre and Miquelon was established on 11 June 1985, replacing its earlier overseas departmental status with a specialised territorial framework under French law. Located off the south coast of Newfoundland, the archipelago is administered by an appointed prefect in Saint-Pierre alongside an elected Territorial Council. The collectivity handles local fishing rights and port services while retaining representation in the French Parliament and access to European development initiatives. \n\n Status: Overseas collectivity of France; Capital and largest city: Saint-Pierre; Official languages: French; Government: Devolved parliamentary local authority; Legislature: Territorial Council; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 11 June 1985; Preceded by: Department of Saint-Pierre and Miquelon; Currency: French franc and Euro

name: Clipperton Island
description: Clipperton Island has been administered since 20 March 1986 as an uninhabited overseas possession under the direct jurisdiction of the French government in Paris. Situated in the eastern Pacific Ocean southwest of Mexico, the coral atoll possesses a massive exclusive economic zone rich in pelagic fisheries and oceanic mineral deposits. The territory functions as a vital site for scientific marine research, weather observation, and international biodiversity monitoring under the French Ministry of the Overseas. \n\n Status: Overseas territory of France; Capital: None (uninhabited); Administrative seat: Paris; Official languages: French; Government: Direct ministerial administration; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 20 March 1986; Preceded by: French Polynesia; Currency: Euro

name: Republic of Côte d'Ivoire
description: The Republic of Cote d'Ivoire formally mandated on 1 May 1986 that its French name be used exclusively in all international diplomacy, prohibiting translations such as Ivory Coast. Centred between the administrative capital of Yamoussoukro and the primary economic hub of Abidjan, the West African state maintained strong agricultural output as a foremost exporter of cocoa and coffee. The republic experienced significant commercial expansion under President Felix Houphouet-Boigny before confronting economic turbulence and political transitions during subsequent decades. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital: Yamoussoukro; Largest city: Abidjan; Official languages: French; Government: Unitary presidential republic; Legislature: Parliament; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 1 May 1986; Preceded by: Republic of Ivory Coast; Currency: West African CFA franc

name: Republic of the Marshall Islands
description: The Republic of the Marshall Islands achieved sovereign statehood on 21 October 1986 upon implementing a Compact of Free Association with the United States, concluding American trusteeship. Administered from Majuro across twenty-nine low-lying atolls and five islands in Micronesia, the nation operates a parliamentary system led by an executive president advised by the Council of Iroij. The island state manages valuable oceanic tuna fisheries and an open international ship registry while relying on bilateral financial agreements with Washington. \n\n Status: Sovereign associated state; Capital and largest city: Majuro; Official languages: Marshallese and English; Government: Unitary parliamentary republic with an executive president; Legislature: Nitijela; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 21 October 1986; Preceded by: Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands; Currency: United States dollar

name: Federated States of Micronesia
description: The Federated States of Micronesia emerged as a sovereign island nation on 3 November 1986 under a Compact of Free Association that ended United States administrative trusteeship. Governed from Palikir on the island of Pohnpei, the federal republic encompasses four distinct island states comprising over six hundred islands across the Caroline archipelago. The government stewards an expansive oceanic territory, balancing local traditional customs with national priorities in commercial fisheries, education, and international climate advocacy. \n\n Status: Sovereign associated state; Capital: Palikir; Largest city: Weno; Official languages: English; Common languages: Chuukese, Pohnpeian and Yapese; Government: Federal assembly-independent republic; Legislature: Congress; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 3 November 1986; Preceded by: Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands; Currency: United States dollar

name: Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands
description: The Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands entered into political union with the United States on 4 November 1986 as an organised unincorporated commonwealth, terminating its United Nations trusteeship status. Centred at Saipan, the fourteen-island archipelago exercises self-government under its own constitution with an elected governor and bicameral legislature. The territory developed an economy driven by Asian tourism, light commerce, and regional transport infrastructure while residents enjoy full United States citizenship. \n\n Status: Unincorporated commonwealth territory of the United States; Capital and largest city: Saipan; Official languages: English, Chamorro and Carolinian; Government: Devolved presidential constitutional dependency; Legislature: Commonwealth Legislature; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 4 November 1986; Preceded by: Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands; Currency: United States dollar

name: People's Democratic Republic of Ethiopia
description: The People's Democratic Republic of Ethiopia was proclaimed on 22 February 1987 following the ratification of a socialist constitution that transformed the ruling military Derg into a civilian one-party state. Headquartered at Addis Ababa under President Mengistu Haile Mariam, the government enforced Marxist-Leninist policies through the Workers' Party of Ethiopia and the National Shengo. Undermined by economic paralysis, catastrophic famines, and armed rebellions in Eritrea and Tigray, the regime collapsed in May 1991 when insurgent armies captured the capital. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Addis Ababa; Official languages: Amharic; Religion: State atheism; Government: Unitary Marxist-Leninist one-party republic; Ruler title: General Secretary; First ruler: Mengistu Haile Mariam; Legislature: National Shengo; Historical era: Cold War; Established: 22 February 1987; Disestablished: 28 May 1991; Preceded by: Provisional Military Government of Socialist Ethiopia; Succeeded by: Transitional Government of Ethiopia; Currency: Ethiopian birr

name: Republic of Chad (Military Occupation)
description: The Republic of Chad (Military Occupation) comprised the forward operational pocket occupied by Chadian military forces inside southern Libya in September 1987 during the Chadian-Libyan War. Commanded by officers loyal to President Hissene Habre, swift Chadian motorised columns launched a surprise offensive that captured the fortified Libyan airbase at Maaten al-Sarra. The forces dismantled military aircraft, captured armaments, and destroyed installations before returning south across the frontier prior to an internationally mediated ceasefire. \n\n Status: Military occupation; Administrative seat: Mobile operational command; Official languages: French and Arabic; Government: Military administration; Historical era: Cold War; Established: 4 September 1987; Disestablished: 11 September 1987; Preceded by: Libyan Arab Jamahiriya; Succeeded by: Libyan Arab Jamahiriya; Currency: Central African CFA franc

name: Republic of Fiji
description: The Republic of Fiji was proclaimed on 6 October 1987 when military leader Sitiveni Rabuka revoked the 1970 constitution following two coups d'état, severing formal ties with the British Crown. Centred at Suva on Viti Levu, the South Pacific island state navigated complex ethnic and political divisions between indigenous Fijians and Indo-Fijians over parliamentary representation. The nation subsequently drafted democratic revisions, rejoined the Commonwealth of Nations, and expanded its key industries in tourism, sugar processing, and mineral extraction. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Suva; Official languages: English, Fijian and Hindi; Government: Unitary parliamentary republic; Legislature: Parliament; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 6 October 1987; Preceded by: Dominion of Fiji; Currency: Fijian dollar

name: Union of Myanmar
description: The Union of Myanmar was established on 18 September 1988 when the military seized direct executive power through the State Law and Order Restoration Council, suppressing the nationwide pro-democracy uprising. Administered from Yangon, the junta changed the country's official name from Burma to Myanmar in 1989 and placed democratic opposition figures under house arrest. The authoritarian military government maintained centralised control over resource extraction and border regions until a new constitution was promulgated in 2008. \n\n Status: Sovereign state under military rule; Capital: Yangon; Official languages: Burmese; Government: Military junta; Head of state: Saw Maung; Historical era: Post-Cold War; Established: 18 September 1988; Disestablished: 10 May 2008; Preceded by: Socialist Republic of the Union of Burma; Succeeded by: Republic of the Union of Myanmar; Currency: Kyat

name: State of Cambodia
description: The State of Cambodia was created on 26 September 1989 as a transitional authority replacing the People's Republic of Kampuchea following the complete withdrawal of Vietnamese military garrisons. Headquartered at Phnom Penh under Prime Minister Hun Sen, the government renounced state socialism, revived private property rights, and reinstated Buddhism as the official religion. The administration cooperated with the United Nations Transitional Authority in Cambodia, facilitating free democratic elections and the restoration of the constitutional monarchy in 1993. \n\n Status: Sovereign transitional state; Capital and largest city: Phnom Penh; Official languages: Khmer; Religion: Buddhism; Government: Transitional parliamentary republic; Legislature: National Assembly; Historical era: Post-Cold War; Established: 26 September 1989; Disestablished: 24 September 1993; Preceded by: People's Republic of Kampuchea; Succeeded by: Kingdom of Cambodia; Currency: Cambodian riel

name: Republic of Hungary
description: The Republic of Hungary was proclaimed on 23 October 1989, ending four decades of communist one-party rule and founding the democratic Third Hungarian Republic. Governed from Budapest, the state adopted sweeping constitutional amendments that instituted a competitive multi-party parliamentary democracy and fostered market-oriented economic reforms. The nation integrated closely into European and transatlantic frameworks, joining NATO in 1999 and the European Union in 2004 before adopting a revised fundamental law in 2012. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Budapest; Official languages: Hungarian; Government: Unitary parliamentary republic; Legislature: National Assembly; Historical era: Post-Cold War; Established: 23 October 1989; Disestablished: 1 January 2012; Preceded by: Hungarian People's Republic; Succeeded by: Hungary; Currency: Forint

name: Romania
description: Romania embarked on a democratic era on 29 December 1989 following the violent overthrow and execution of communist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu during the Romanian Revolution. Guided from Bucharest by the National Salvation Front, the Southeastern European state adopted a new democratic constitution in 1991 establishing a semi-presidential republic. The nation carried out complex economic transitions, gradually modernising its agricultural and industrial base to achieve full integration into NATO in 2004 and the European Union in 2007. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Bucharest; Official languages: Romanian; Government: Unitary semi-presidential republic; Legislature: Parliament; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 29 December 1989; Preceded by: Socialist Republic of Romania; Currency: Romanian leu

name: Republic of Poland
description: The Republic of Poland was formally reinstated on 31 December 1989 when constitutional amendments expunged the socialist title of the Polish People's Republic, establishing the Third Polish Republic. Centred at Warsaw, the parliamentary democracy implemented sweeping market reforms known as the Balcerowicz Plan to stabilise the economy after decades of command planning. Poland became an influential Central European economic power and security anchor on NATO's eastern frontier, subsequently joining the European Union in 2004. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Warsaw; Official languages: Polish; Government: Unitary parliamentary republic; Legislature: Parliament; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 31 December 1989; Preceded by: Polish People's Republic; Currency: Zloty

name: Republic of Benin
description: The Republic of Benin was inaugurated on 1 March 1990 after a landmark national conference successfully dismantled Mathieu Kerekou's Marxist-Leninist regime in favour of constitutional pluralism. Administered from Porto-Novo with its governmental headquarters in Cotonou, the West African state became an early pioneer of peaceful multi-party democratic transitions on the African continent. The nation maintained political stability while cultivating agricultural commerce, port logistics, and regional trade connections across the Gulf of Guinea. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital: Porto-Novo; Largest city: Cotonou; Official languages: French; Government: Unitary presidential republic; Legislature: National Assembly; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 1 March 1990; Preceded by: People's Republic of Benin; Currency: West African CFA franc

name: Republic of Namibia
description: The Republic of Namibia achieved sovereign independence on 21 March 1990, concluding seventy-five years of South African rule and bringing an end to the prolonged Namibian War of Independence. Headquartered at Windhoek, the newly established state enacted a progressive constitution that abolished all apartheid-era homelands and safeguarded fundamental civil rights. The country built a resilient multi-party democracy and fostered economic growth through mineral extraction, commercial fisheries, and eco-tourism, successfully reintegrating Walvis Bay in 1994. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Windhoek; Official languages: English; Government: Unitary semi-presidential republic; Legislature: Parliament; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 21 March 1990; Preceded by: South West Africa; Currency: Namibian dollar and South African rand

name: Czech and Slovak Federative Republic
description: The Czech and Slovak Federative Republic was established on 23 April 1990, succeeding the Czechoslovak Socialist Republic following the peaceful triumph of the Velvet Revolution. Centred at Prague under the presidency of Vaclav Havel, the federal state dismantled communist control, rehabilitated civil liberties, and embraced free-market economic principles. Despite shared democratic ideals, diverging regional political goals culminated in the peaceful dissolution of the federation on 31 December 1992, creating the independent Czech and Slovak republics. \n\n Status: Federal sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Prague; Official languages: Czech and Slovak; Government: Federal parliamentary republic; Head of state: Václav Havel; Legislature: Federal Assembly; Historical era: Post-Cold War; Established: 23 April 1990; Disestablished: 31 December 1992; Preceded by: Czechoslovak Socialist Republic; Succeeded by: Czech Republic and Slovakia; Currency: Czechoslovak koruna

name: Republic of Yemen
description: The Republic of Yemen was established on 22 May 1990 through the historic unification of North Yemen and South Yemen, ending decades of ideological and geopolitical division. Governed from Sana'a under President Ali Abdullah Saleh, the state united conservative tribal regions and former socialist institutions across the southern Arabian Peninsula. Although challenged by a brief civil war in 1994 and devastating regional conflicts after 2014, the republic has remained the internationally recognised government representing Yemeni statehood. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Sana'a; Official languages: Arabic; Religion: Islam; Government: Unitary presidential republic; Legislature: Parliament; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 22 May 1990; Preceded by: Yemen Arab Republic and People's Democratic Republic of Yemen; Currency: Yemeni rial

name: Pridnestrovian Moldavian Soviet Socialist Republic
description: The Pridnestrovian Moldavian Soviet Socialist Republic was proclaimed on 2 September 1990 by pro-Soviet separatists on the left bank of the Dniester River, resisting Moldovan independence and potential unification with Romania. Headquartered at Tiraspol under Igor Smirnov, the self-proclaimed entity sought recognition as a distinct constituent republic within the Soviet Union. The administration controlled industrial facilities and administrative centres until the final collapse of the USSR, prompting it to declare full independence as the Pridnestrovian Moldavian Republic in August 1991. \n\n Status: Unrecognised Soviet republic; Capital and largest city: Tiraspol; Common languages: Russian, Moldovan and Ukrainian; Government: Provisional Soviet republic; Head of state: Igor Smirnov; Legislature: Supreme Soviet; Historical era: Dissolution of the Soviet Union; Established: 2 September 1990; Disestablished: 25 August 1991; Preceded by: Moldavian Soviet Socialist Republic; Succeeded by: Pridnestrovian Moldavian Republic; Currency: Soviet ruble

name: Rwandan Patriotic Front
description: The Rwandan Patriotic Front was an armed insurgent movement formed by exiled Tutsi refugees in Uganda who launched an invasion of northern Rwanda in October 1990. Operating without a fixed capital from mobile mountain camps in the Virunga region under the leadership of Paul Kagame, the movement challenged the government of Juvenal Habyarimana during the Rwandan Civil War. In response to the 1994 Rwandan genocide, the front launched a decisive offensive that captured Kigali in July 1994, halting the mass killings and forming a national unity government. \n\n Status: Insurgent military movement; Administrative seat: Mobile military command; Common languages: Kinyarwanda, English and French; Government: Rebel military administration; Head of state: Paul Kagame; Historical era: Post-Cold War; Established: 5 October 1990; Disestablished: 18 July 1994; Preceded by: Republic of Rwanda; Succeeded by: Republic of Rwanda; Historical region: Great Lakes Africa

name: Republic of Mozambique
description: The Republic of Mozambique adopted a democratic constitution on 30 November 1990, relinquishing its Marxist-Leninist title and establishing a multi-party political system. Governed from Maputo, the state concluded the Rome General Peace Accords in 1992, successfully ending sixteen years of destructive civil war against RENAMO insurgents. The nation subsequently conducted democratic elections, rebuilt transportation corridors, and harnessed agricultural and natural gas wealth along its extensive Indian Ocean coastline. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Maputo; Official languages: Portuguese; Government: Unitary semi-presidential republic; Legislature: Assembly of the Republic; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 30 November 1990; Preceded by: People's Republic of Mozambique; Currency: Mozambican metical

name: Republic of South Ossetia - the State of Alania
description: The Republic of South Ossetia - the State of Alania declared independence from Georgia in late 1991 during the collapse of the Soviet Union, establishing a de facto breakaway state in the South Caucasus. Headquartered at Tskhinvali, the republic resisted Georgian central authority during the 1991-1992 conflict and consolidated its separation following the 2008 Russo-Georgian War. The state is diplomatically recognised by Russia and a handful of other nations, whilst remaining internationally viewed by most sovereign governments as an integral part of Georgia. \n\n Status: Partially recognised sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Tskhinvali; Official languages: Ossetian and Russian; Government: Unitary semi-presidential republic; Legislature: Parliament; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 28 November 1991; Preceded by: South Ossetian Autonomous Oblast; Currency: Russian ruble

name: Federal Republic of Somalia
description: The Federal Republic of Somalia was reconstituted after the ouster of dictator Siad Barre in January 1991, which fractured the Horn of Africa nation into prolonged civil war and regional strife. Administered from Mogadishu, successive transitional administrations and the subsequent federal authority worked to reconstruct national institutions while combating persistent extremist insurgencies. The federal structure incorporates autonomous regional member states across the country, while navigating the de facto independence of Somaliland along its northern coast. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Mogadishu; Official languages: Somali and Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Federal parliamentary republic; Legislature: Federal Parliament; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 26 January 1991; Preceded by: Somali Democratic Republic; Currency: Somali shilling

name: Gulf War Coalition (Military Occupation)
description: The Gulf War Coalition (Military Occupation) comprised the operational command and temporary security zone established across liberated Kuwait and occupied southern Iraq by multi-national forces during the 1991 Gulf War. Administered from expeditionary military headquarters without a permanent civilian capital, the allied forces executed Operation Desert Storm under United Nations mandates to repel the Iraqi occupation. The command secured strategic transport corridors and established demilitarised zones along the border before handing authority back to Kuwait and withdrawing in May 1991. \n\n Status: Military coalition operational command; Administrative seat: Mobile coalition headquarters; Common languages: English and Arabic; Government: Multi-national military command; Historical era: Post-Cold War; Established: 26 February 1991; Disestablished: 1 May 1991; Preceded by: Republic of Iraq; Succeeded by: State of Kuwait and Republic of Iraq; Currency: United States dollar

name: Republic of Georgia
description: The Republic of Georgia declared its independence from the Soviet Union on 9 April 1991 following a popular national referendum led by dissident Zviad Gamsakhurdia. Governed from Tbilisi, the early South Caucasus republic was soon shaken by a violent coup d'état, severe economic disruption, and armed separatist conflicts in South Ossetia and Abkhazia. Under the leadership of Eduard Shevardnadze, the country established institutional stability, culminating in the adoption of a new democratic constitution in August 1995 that renamed the state simply as Georgia. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Tbilisi; Official languages: Georgian; Government: Unitary semi-presidential republic; Head of state: Zviad Gamsakhurdia; Legislature: Parliament; Historical era: Post-Cold War; Established: 9 April 1991; Disestablished: 24 August 1995; Preceded by: Georgian Soviet Socialist Republic; Succeeded by: Georgia; Currency: Georgian coupon and Ruble

name: Afghan Interim Government
description: The Afghan Interim Government was established in April 1991 by a coalition of seven major mujahideen factions seeking to coordinate military and political campaigns against the Soviet-backed regime in Kabul. Operating without a permanent domestic capital from cross-border operational centres near Peshawar and liberated rural valleys, the alliance struggled with severe ideological and ethnic tensions. The coalition achieved its objective when insurgent units entered Kabul in April 1992, transitioning power under the Peshawar Accords to the new Islamic State of Afghanistan. \n\n Status: Insurgent provisional government; Administrative seat: Peshawar; Official languages: Pashto and Dari; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Mujahideen provisional coalition; Ruler title: President; First ruler: Sibghatullah Mojaddedi; Historical era: Afghan conflict; Established: 11 April 1991; Disestablished: 26 April 1992; Preceded by: Republic of Afghanistan; Succeeded by: Islamic State of Afghanistan; Currency: Afghan afghani

name: Republic of Somaliland
description: The Republic of Somaliland unilaterally declared its independence from Somalia on 18 May 1991, dissolving the 1960 union following the collapse of the central government in Mogadishu. Headquartered at Hargeisa, the de facto sovereign state established a peaceful and functioning constitutional democracy within the historical frontiers of the British Somaliland protectorate. The republic maintains its own elected parliament, separate armed forces, and national currency, continuing to seek broad international recognition while sustaining robust regional trade. \n\n Status: De facto independent state with limited recognition; Capital and largest city: Hargeisa; Official languages: Somali and Arabic; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Unitary presidential republic; Legislature: Parliament; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 18 May 1991; Preceded by: Somali Democratic Republic; Currency: Somaliland shilling

name: Transitional Government of Ethiopia
description: The Transitional Government of Ethiopia was instituted on 28 May 1991 following the capture of Addis Ababa by the Ethiopian People's Revolutionary Democratic Front and the fall of the Marxist Derg regime. Guided by President Meles Zenawi, the transitional administration recognised the de facto separation of Eritrea and restructured Ethiopia's historical administrative provinces along ethnolinguistic boundaries. The transitional period laid the foundation for the 1995 federal constitution, establishing the modern Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia. \n\n Status: Sovereign transitional government; Capital and largest city: Addis Ababa; Official languages: Amharic; Government: Transitional parliamentary republic; Head of state: Meles Zenawi; Historical era: Post-Cold War; Established: 28 May 1991; Disestablished: 21 August 1995; Preceded by: People's Democratic Republic of Ethiopia; Succeeded by: Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia; Currency: Ethiopian birr

name: State of Eritrea
description: The State of Eritrea established de facto sovereignty on 29 May 1991 when the Eritrean People's Liberation Front liberated Asmara, which was confirmed by an internationally monitored independence referendum in 1993. Administered from Asmara under President Isaias Afwerki, the Red Sea nation organised its institutions around a single-party presidential framework with compulsory national service. The country defended its frontiers during a bitter border war with Ethiopia between 1998 and 2000, maintaining a self-reliant economic and defence policy. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Asmara; Official languages: Tigrinya, Arabic and English; Government: Unitary one-party presidential republic; Ruler title: President; First ruler: Isaias Afwerki; Legislature: National Assembly; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 29 May 1991; Preceded by: People's Democratic Republic of Ethiopia; Currency: Eritrean nakfa and Ethiopian birr

name: Republic of Croatia
description: The Republic of Croatia declared sovereign statehood on 25 June 1991, concluding its participation in the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia after a decisive public vote. Governed from Zagreb, the fledgling state fought the Croatian War of Independence against rebel Serb forces and the Yugoslav military, restoring full territorial integrity by 1995. Croatia built an enduring parliamentary democracy, gaining entry to NATO in 2009 and the European Union in 2013 while developing a renowned maritime tourism and manufacturing economy along the Adriatic Sea. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Zagreb; Official languages: Croatian; Government: Unitary parliamentary republic; Legislature: Sabor; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 25 June 1991; Preceded by: Socialist Republic of Croatia; Currency: Croatian kuna and Euro

name: Republic of Slovenia
description: The Republic of Slovenia proclaimed its sovereign independence on 25 June 1991, successfully repelling federal intervention during the brief Ten-Day War against the Yugoslav People's Army. Administered from Ljubljana, the Alpine nation established a progressive parliamentary democracy and instituted comprehensive economic reforms. Slovenia became the first former Yugoslav republic to integrate into Western institutions, joining both the European Union and NATO in 2004 while maintaining advanced manufacturing and high living standards. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Ljubljana; Official languages: Slovene; Government: Unitary parliamentary republic; Legislature: Parliament; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 25 June 1991; Preceded by: Socialist Republic of Slovenia; Currency: Slovenian tolar and Euro

name: Serbian Autonomous Oblast of Eastern Slavonia, Baranja and Western Syrmia
description: The Serbian Autonomous Oblast of Eastern Slavonia, Baranja and Western Syrmia was declared on 25 June 1991 as an insurgent Serb territory along the Danube river basin in eastern Croatia. Centred at Vukovar following the city's destructive capture by Yugoslav forces, the local authority expelled non-Serb residents and established armed militias with backing from Belgrade. The entity functioned as a provisional regional regime until officially merging into the Republic of Serbian Krajina in February 1992. \n\n Status: Unrecognised insurgent quasi-state; Capital: Vukovar; Common languages: Serbian and Croatian; Government: Provisional rebel administration; Historical era: Breakup of Yugoslavia; Established: 25 June 1991; Disestablished: 26 February 1992; Preceded by: Republic of Croatia; Succeeded by: Republic of Serbian Krajina; Currency: Krajina dinar

name: Serbian Autonomous Oblast of Krajina
description: The Serbian Autonomous Oblast of Krajina functioned as a self-declared Serb territory within the Knin and Lika regions of Croatia, having proclaimed autonomy prior to Croatia's independence declaration in June 1991. Headquartered at Knin under Milan Babic, the entity mobilised armed local units and took control of strategic transport routes with assistance from the Yugoslav military. In December 1991, the leadership consolidated with adjacent Serb-held enclaves to proclaim the Republic of Serbian Krajina. \n\n Status: Unrecognised insurgent region; Capital: Knin; Common languages: Serbian; Government: Provisional rebel administration; Historical era: Breakup of Yugoslavia; Established: 21 December 1990; Disestablished: 19 December 1991; Preceded by: Socialist Republic of Croatia; Succeeded by: Republic of Serbian Krajina; Currency: Yugoslav dinar

name: Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia (Military Occupation)
description: The Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia (Military Occupation) comprised the operational theatre held by the Yugoslav People's Army across Slovenia during the Ten-Day War in late June and early July 1991. Commanded directly by military headquarters in Belgrade without an established civil seat, federal mechanised units moved to secure international frontier posts and airports. Met by determined armed resistance from Slovenian forces and European diplomatic mediation, the Yugoslav military agreed to a total troop withdrawal. \n\n Status: Military occupation; Administrative seat: Mobile operational field command; Official languages: Serbo-Croatian and Slovene; Government: Military administration; Historical era: Breakup of Yugoslavia; Established: 27 June 1991; Disestablished: 6 July 1991; Preceded by: Republic of Slovenia; Succeeded by: Republic of Slovenia; Currency: Yugoslav dinar

name: Republic of Bulgaria
description: The Republic of Bulgaria was established on 12 July 1991 upon the adoption of a democratic constitution by the Grand National Assembly, ending decades of communist one-party rule. Headquartered at Sofia, the Balkan state dismantled socialist command economic structures in favour of private enterprise and open-market principles. The country successfully integrated into transatlantic and European institutions, becoming a member of NATO in 2004 and the European Union in 2007. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Sofia; Official languages: Bulgarian; Religion: Eastern Orthodoxy; Government: Unitary parliamentary republic; Legislature: National Assembly; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 12 July 1991; Preceded by: People's Republic of Bulgaria; Currency: Bulgarian lev

name: Serbian Autonomous Oblast of Western Slavonia
description: The Serbian Autonomous Oblast of Western Slavonia was proclaimed on 12 August 1991 as an insurgent Serb enclave in central Croatia resisting Croatian independence. Centred at Pakrac, the breakaway administration maintained armed checkpoints and coordinated paramilitary operations alongside regular Yugoslav forces. Following intense combat and major territorial losses during Croatian offensive operations in late 1991, the remaining territory was incorporated into the Republic of Serbian Krajina in January 1992. \n\n Status: Unrecognised insurgent quasi-state; Capital: Pakrac; Common languages: Serbian and Croatian; Government: Provisional rebel administration; Historical era: Breakup of Yugoslavia; Established: 12 August 1991; Disestablished: 5 January 1992; Preceded by: Republic of Croatia; Succeeded by: Republic of Serbian Krajina; Currency: Yugoslav dinar

name: Ukraine
description: Ukraine declared sovereign statehood on 24 August 1991, which was confirmed by an overwhelming national referendum that catalysed the formal dissolution of the Soviet Union. Governed from Kyiv, the expansive Eastern European democracy surrendered its inherited Soviet nuclear arsenal under the 1994 Budapest Memorandum in exchange for international security assurances. The nation developed major agricultural and metallurgy industries, while resolutely defending its sovereignty, democratic institutions, and European integration against Russian military aggression. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Kyiv; Official languages: Ukrainian; Religion: Eastern Orthodoxy; Government: Unitary semi-presidential republic; Legislature: Verkhovna Rada; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 24 August 1991; Preceded by: Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic; Currency: Ukrainian hryvnia

name: Pridnestrovian Moldavian Republic
description: The Pridnestrovian Moldavian Republic was proclaimed on 25 August 1991 as an unrecognised breakaway state along the eastern bank of the Dniester River, separating from newly independent Moldova. Governed from Tiraspol, the pro-Russian separatist entity consolidated control following the brief War of Transnistria in 1992, supported by Russian military units stationed locally. The territory maintains its own constitution, parliament, armed forces, and financial institutions while remaining internationally recognised as sovereign Moldovan territory. \n\n Status: Unrecognised de facto state; Capital and largest city: Tiraspol; Official languages: Russian, Moldovan and Ukrainian; Government: Unitary semi-presidential republic; Legislature: Supreme Council; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 25 August 1991; Preceded by: Pridnestrovian Moldavian Soviet Socialist Republic; Currency: Transnistrian ruble

name: Republic of Belarus
description: The Republic of Belarus became an independent sovereign state on 25 August 1991 as the Soviet Union collapsed, subsequently co-founding the Commonwealth of Independent States. Centred at Minsk, the landlocked nation preserved extensive state ownership across its manufacturing and agricultural sectors under the long-standing presidency of Aleksandr Lukashenko. The country maintained deep political, economic, and defence alignments with the Russian Federation, formalised through the bilateral Union State agreement. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Minsk; Official languages: Belarusian and Russian; Government: Unitary presidential republic under authoritarian governance; Legislature: National Assembly; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 25 August 1991; Preceded by: Byelorussian Soviet Socialist Republic; Currency: Belarusian ruble

name: Republic of Moldova
description: The Republic of Moldova declared sovereign independence from the USSR on 27 August 1991, establishing a democratic state between Romania and Ukraine. Administered from Chisinau, the fledgling republic was quickly confronted by the armed secession of the pro-Russian Transnistria region along the Dniester River in 1992. The country cultivated an economy focused on viticulture and agriculture, while pursuing deeper structural reforms and candidate status within the European Union. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Chișinău; Official languages: Romanian; Religion: Eastern Orthodoxy; Government: Unitary parliamentary republic; Legislature: Parliament; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 27 August 1991; Preceded by: Moldavian Soviet Socialist Republic; Currency: Moldovan leu

name: Republic of Azerbaijan
description: The Republic of Azerbaijan proclaimed its restored sovereignty on 30 August 1991, ending seven decades of Soviet rule in the South Caucasus. Headquartered at Baku on the Caspian Sea, the nation was immediately plunged into the First Nagorno-Karabakh War against Armenian separatist forces. Under the leadership of Heydar Aliyev and Ilham Aliyev, Azerbaijan utilised massive offshore oil and natural gas revenues to modernise infrastructure, eventually restoring full territorial control over Nagorno-Karabakh by 2023. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Baku; Official languages: Azerbaijani; Religion: Islam; Government: Unitary semi-presidential republic; Legislature: National Assembly; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 30 August 1991; Preceded by: Azerbaijan Soviet Socialist Republic; Currency: Azerbaijani manat

name: Republic of Kyrgyzstan
description: The Republic of Kyrgyzstan served as the official constitutional designation of independent Kyrgyzstan following its declaration of sovereignty from the Soviet Union on 31 August 1991. Centred at Bishkek under President Askar Akayev, the mountainous Central Asian state initiated structural economic reforms and created democratic public institutions. This foundational period concluded on 5 May 1993 with the adoption of a comprehensive constitution, which formally established the sovereign state as the Kyrgyz Republic. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Bishkek; Official languages: Kyrgyz and Russian; Government: Unitary presidential republic; Ruler title: President; First ruler: Askar Akayev; Historical era: Post-Cold War; Established: 31 August 1991; Disestablished: 5 May 1993; Preceded by: Kirghiz Soviet Socialist Republic; Succeeded by: Kyrgyz Republic; Currency: Soviet ruble and Russian ruble

name: Republic of Uzbekistan
description: The Republic of Uzbekistan proclaimed sovereign statehood on 1 September 1991 as Soviet central authority disintegrated, ending its status as a Soviet republic. Governed from Tashkent under President Islam Karimov, the doubly landlocked Central Asian nation implemented measured economic reforms while retaining strong central controls over cotton production and mineral extraction. The republic subsequently modernised its industrial base and played a prominent diplomatic role across the historic Silk Road region. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Tashkent; Official languages: Uzbek; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Unitary presidential republic; Legislature: Oliy Majlis; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 1 September 1991; Preceded by: Uzbek Soviet Socialist Republic; Currency: Uzbek som

name: Nagorno-Karabakh Republic
description: The Nagorno-Karabakh Republic was proclaimed on 2 September 1991 by Armenian deputies across the former Nagorno-Karabakh Autonomous Oblast as the Soviet Union collapsed. Headquartered at Stepanakert, the unrecognised breakaway entity fought the First Nagorno-Karabakh War against Azerbaijan, securing control over the mountainous enclave and surrounding buffer territories. The de facto state maintained separate governing and defence institutions until adopting the formal name Republic of Artsakh through a constitutional referendum in 2017. \n\n Status: Unrecognised de facto state; Capital and largest city: Stepanakert; Official languages: Armenian; Religion: Armenian Apostolic Christianity; Government: Semi-presidential republic; Legislature: National Assembly; Historical era: Post-Cold War; Established: 2 September 1991; Disestablished: 21 February 2017; Preceded by: Nagorno-Karabakh Autonomous Oblast; Succeeded by: Republic of Artsakh; Currency: Armenian dram

name: All-National Congress of the Chechen People
description: The All-National Congress of the Chechen People functioned as the revolutionary governing movement that took control in Grozny in September 1991, unseating the local Soviet administration. Led by former Soviet Air Force general Dzhokhar Dudayev, the congress mobilised armed volunteers and organised mass public rallies to demand complete separation from Russia. The movement organised presidential and parliamentary elections that culminated in the formal declaration of the Chechen Republic of Ichkeria in November 1991. \n\n Status: Revolutionary provisional authority; Capital: Grozny; Official languages: Chechen and Russian; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Revolutionary council; Head of state: Dzhokhar Dudayev; Historical era: Dissolution of the Soviet Union; Established: 6 September 1991; Disestablished: 1 November 1991; Preceded by: Checheno-Ingush ASSR; Succeeded by: Chechen Republic of Ichkeria; Currency: Soviet ruble

name: Republic of Macedonia
description: The Republic of Macedonia achieved sovereign independence on 8 September 1991 following a peaceful national referendum that withdrew the territory from the disintegrating Yugoslav federation. Administered from Skopje, the landlocked Balkan state avoided the destructive conflicts affecting neighbouring republics, later negotiating the 2001 Ohrid Framework Agreement to guarantee minority rights. The nation operated under this name until February 2019, when the historic Prespa Agreement with Greece took effect, establishing the Republic of North Macedonia. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Skopje; Official languages: Macedonian; Government: Unitary parliamentary republic; Legislature: Assembly; Historical era: Post-Cold War; Established: 8 September 1991; Disestablished: 12 February 2019; Preceded by: Socialist Republic of Macedonia; Succeeded by: Republic of North Macedonia; Currency: Macedonian denar

name: Republic of Tajikistan
description: The Republic of Tajikistan declared sovereign statehood on 9 September 1991 during the collapse of the Soviet Union. Centred at Dushanbe, the mountainous nation was soon engulfed by a brutal civil war between regional, democratic, and Islamist forces that lasted until a United Nations-brokered peace agreement in 1997. Under President Emomali Rahmon, the state consolidated centralised political authority, developing aluminium manufacturing, hydroelectric infrastructure, and agricultural commerce. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Dushanbe; Official languages: Tajik and Russian; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Unitary presidential republic; Legislature: Supreme Assembly; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 9 September 1991; Preceded by: Tajik Soviet Socialist Republic; Currency: Tajikistani somoni

name: Republic of Armenia
description: The Republic of Armenia proclaimed its sovereign independence on 23 September 1991 following a national referendum that confirmed its departure from the collapsing Soviet Union. Governed from Yerevan in the South Caucasus highlands, the landlocked nation endured a severe trade blockade while supporting ethnic Armenians in the First Nagorno-Karabakh War. The country developed a parliamentary democracy with active technology, mining, and agricultural sectors, bolstered by strong cultural links with its international diaspora. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Yerevan; Official languages: Armenian; Religion: Armenian Apostolic Christianity; Government: Unitary parliamentary republic; Legislature: National Assembly; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 23 September 1991; Preceded by: Armenian Soviet Socialist Republic; Currency: Armenian dram

name: Dubrovnik Republic
description: The Dubrovnik Republic was an unrecognised quasi-state proclaimed on 15 October 1991 by local Serb politicians backed by the Yugoslav People's Army during the Siege of Dubrovnik. Headquartered de facto at Cavtat under Aleksandar Apolonio, the administration attempted to revive the historic heritage of Ragusa as a distinct regional entity within a reduced Yugoslavia. The puppet administration failed to secure local civic support and completely dissolved when Croatian forces liberated the area in mid-1992. \n\n Status: Unrecognised client quasi-state; Capital: Cavtat (de facto) and Dubrovnik (de jure); Common languages: Serbian and Croatian; Government: Military-backed provisional administration; Head of state: Aleksandar Apolonio; Historical era: Yugoslav Wars; Established: 15 October 1991; Disestablished: 21 June 1992; Preceded by: Republic of Croatia; Succeeded by: Republic of Croatia; Currency: Yugoslav dinar

name: Turkmenistan
description: Turkmenistan declared sovereign independence on 27 October 1991 as the Soviet Union disintegrated, establishing an independent state across the Karakum Desert. Headquartered at Ashgabat, the Central Asian nation was governed by Saparmurat Niyazov, who introduced an extensive personal cult and established a policy of permanent positive neutrality recognised by the United Nations. The government financed expansive civic monuments and welfare subsidies through its colossal natural gas reserves, maintaining strict state controls over public life. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Ashgabat; Official languages: Turkmen; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Unitary presidential republic under authoritarian governance; Legislature: Assembly; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 27 October 1991; Preceded by: Turkmen Soviet Socialist Republic; Currency: Turkmen manat

name: Chechen Republic of Ichkeria
description: The Chechen Republic of Ichkeria declared sovereign independence from Russia on 1 November 1991 under President Dzhokhar Dudayev following the collapse of Soviet institutions in the North Caucasus. Centred at Grozny, the de facto state successfully repelled Russian armed forces during the First Chechen War of 1994-1996 to secure temporary autonomy under the Khasavyurt Accord. However, subsequent economic collapse and the spread of Islamist insurgencies precipitated the Second Chechen War in 1999, which culminated in the Russian capture of Grozny in 2000. \n\n Status: Unrecognised de facto state; Capital and largest city: Grozny; Official languages: Chechen and Russian; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Unitary semi-presidential republic; Ruler title: President; First ruler: Dzhokhar Dudayev; Legislature: Parliament; Historical era: Post-Cold War; Established: 1 November 1991; Disestablished: 31 May 2000; Preceded by: Checheno-Ingush ASSR; Succeeded by: Chechen Republic; Currency: Russian ruble and Chechen naxar

name: Russian Federation
description: The Russian Federation emerged as an independent sovereign republic on 12 December 1991 upon ratifying the Belovezha Accords, assuming the international legal personality and United Nations Security Council seat of the dissolving Soviet Union. Governed from Moscow, the vast transcontinental state weathered difficult market transitions and political instability during the 1990s. Under President Vladimir Putin, the country reasserted centralised state control, strengthened its armed forces, and expanded international influence powered by immense hydrocarbon and mineral wealth. \n\n Status: Sovereign federal state; Capital and largest city: Moscow; Official languages: Russian; Government: Federal semi-presidential republic; Legislature: Federal Assembly; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 12 December 1991; Preceded by: Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic; Currency: Russian ruble

name: Baikonur Cosmodrome
description: The Baikonur Cosmodrome has operated since 16 December 1991 as a Russian-leased aerospace enclave located inside sovereign Kazakhstan following the breakup of the Soviet Union. Centred at the administrative town of Baikonur in the Kazakh steppe, the vast space launch facility is managed jointly by Roscosmos and the Russian military under long-term bilateral lease treaties. The installation serves as the primary operational spaceport for crewed orbital spaceflights to the International Space Station and commercial satellite launches. \n\n Status: Leased administrative territory under Russian jurisdiction; Administrative seat: Baikonur; Official languages: Russian and Kazakh; Government: Special civil-military administration under bilateral lease; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 16 December 1991; Preceded by: Soviet Union; Currency: Russian ruble

name: Republic of Kazakhstan
description: The Republic of Kazakhstan declared sovereign statehood on 16 December 1991 as the final Soviet republic to withdraw from the collapsing USSR. Encompassing vast steppe, mountains, and Caspian coastline, the nation moved its capital from Almaty to Astana in 1997 under long-serving President Nursultan Nazarbayev. The state preserved inter-ethnic harmony, pursued balanced multi-vector foreign relations, and became Central Asia's leading economy through extensive petroleum, uranium, and mineral extraction. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital: Astana; Largest city: Almaty; Official languages: Kazakh and Russian; Government: Unitary presidential republic; Legislature: Parliament; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 16 December 1991; Preceded by: Kazakh Soviet Socialist Republic; Currency: Kazakhstani tenge

name: Republic of Serbian Krajina
description: The Republic of Serbian Krajina was proclaimed on 19 December 1991 through the unification of Serb autonomous enclaves in Croatia, defying the newly independent Croatian republic. Headquartered at Knin under Milan Babic and subsequently Goran Hadzic, the unrecognised quasi-state controlled nearly a third of Croatia with arms and logistical aid from Belgrade. The militarised entity persisted through four years of conflict until August 1995, when Croatian armed forces launched Operation Storm, rapidly recapturing the territory. \n\n Status: Unrecognised client quasi-state; Capital: Knin; Largest city: Vukovar; Common languages: Serbian; Religion: Serbian Orthodoxy; Government: Semi-presidential republic; Head of state: Milan Babić; Legislature: National Assembly; Historical era: Yugoslav Wars; Established: 19 December 1991; Disestablished: 8 August 1995; Preceded by: SAO Krajina; Succeeded by: Republic of Croatia; Currency: Krajina dinar and Yugoslav dinar

name: Republic of Madagascar
description: The Republic of Madagascar was established on 12 January 1992 upon the promulgation of a democratic constitution that ended seventeen years of socialist one-party governance. Governed from Antananarivo across the massive Indian Ocean island, the state introduced competitive multi-party elections and open-market economic policies. The country preserves unique endemic ecosystems while developing an economy focused on agricultural trade, vanilla production, mineral extraction, and international eco-tourism. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Antananarivo; Official languages: Malagasy and French; Government: Unitary semi-presidential republic; Legislature: Parliament; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 12 January 1992; Preceded by: Democratic Republic of Madagascar; Currency: Malagasy ariary

name: Mongolia
description: Mongolia adopted a new democratic constitution on 12 February 1992, removing the People's Republic moniker and concluding seven decades of Soviet-aligned socialist rule. Centred at Ulaanbaatar on the vast plateau between Russia and China, the landlocked democracy established competitive multi-party governance and market economic structures. The nation developed a Third Neighbour foreign policy to diversify international partnerships while expanding copper, coal, and cashmere exports to support its growing urban and nomadic populations. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Ulaanbaatar; Official languages: Mongolian; Religion: Tibetan Buddhism; Government: Unitary semi-presidential republic; Legislature: State Great Khural; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 12 February 1992; Preceded by: Mongolian People's Republic; Currency: Tugrik

name: Croatian Republic of Herzeg-Bosnia
description: The Croatian Republic of Herzeg-Bosnia was an unrecognised Bosnian Croat quasi-state established in south-western Bosnia and Herzegovina during the breakup of Yugoslavia. Governed from Mostar under Mate Boban, the entity's military wing, the Croatian Defence Council, fought both Serb forces and the Bosnian Army during the Croat-Bosniak War. Following diplomatic mediation led by the United States, the leadership signed the 1994 Washington Agreement, which dismantled the entity to create the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina. \n\n Status: Unrecognised insurgent quasi-state; Capital and largest city: Mostar; Official languages: Croatian; Religion: Roman Catholicism; Government: Republic; Head of state: Mate Boban; Legislature: Assembly of Herzeg-Bosnia; Historical era: Yugoslav Wars; Established: 18 November 1991; Disestablished: 18 March 1994; Preceded by: Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina; Succeeded by: Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina; Currency: Croatian dinar and Deutsche Mark

name: Republika Srpska
description: Republika Srpska was established in early 1992 by Bosnian Serb leaders who opposed the independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, functioning as a de facto independent state throughout the Bosnian War. Headquartered at Pale with its administrative centre at Banja Luka, the entity was led by Radovan Karadzic and supported by the Army of Republika Srpska. The war ended with the 1995 Dayton Agreement, which formally recognised Republika Srpska as one of two autonomous constituent entities within Bosnia and Herzegovina. \n\n Status: Unrecognised breakaway state; Capital: Sarajevo (de jure) and Banja Luka (de facto); Official languages: Serbian; Religion: Serbian Orthodoxy; Government: Semi-presidential republic; Head of state: Radovan Karadžić; Legislature: National Assembly; Historical era: Yugoslav Wars; Established: 28 February 1992; Disestablished: 14 December 1995; Preceded by: Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina; Succeeded by: Bosnia and Herzegovina (Republika Srpska entity); Currency: Republika Srpska dinar

name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
description: Bosnia and Herzegovina declared sovereign statehood on 3 March 1992 following an independence referendum, immediately descending into the catastrophic Bosnian War. Governed from the besieged capital of Sarajevo under President Alija Izetbegovic, the republic defended its sovereignty against separate Serb and Croat breakaway quasi-states. Following the 1995 Dayton Peace Accords, the nation was reconstituted as a decentralised federal democratic republic consisting of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Republika Srpska under a tripartite presidency. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Sarajevo; Official languages: Bosnian, Croatian and Serbian; Government: Federal parliamentary directorial republic; Head of state: Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina; Legislature: Parliamentary Assembly; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 3 March 1992; Preceded by: Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina; Currency: Convertible mark

name: Republic of Mauritius
description: The Republic of Mauritius was established on 12 March 1992 when the Indian Ocean island nation adopted a republican constitution, replacing the British monarch with an elected ceremonial president. Administered from Port Louis, the country developed into one of Africa's most prosperous and politically stable democracies. The nation successfully transitioned from single-crop sugar cultivation into a diversified modern economy driven by textile manufacturing, financial services, and high-end beach tourism. \n\n Status: Sovereign state; Capital and largest city: Port Louis; Official languages: English and French; Common languages: Mauritian Creole; Government: Unitary parliamentary republic; Legislature: National Assembly; Historical era: Contemporary; Established: 12 March 1992; Preceded by: Mauritius; Currency: Mauritian rupee

name: Islamic State of Afghanistan
description: The Islamic State of Afghanistan was proclaimed on 26 April 1992 under the Peshawar Accord following the collapse of the communist regime in Kabul, uniting diverse mujahideen parties under President Burhanuddin Rabbani. The fledgling Islamic state immediately faced destructive factional fighting between rival warlords, devastating Kabul and creating conditions for the rapid emergence of the Taliban. Expelled from the capital in 1996, the government led the anti-Taliban Northern Alliance from northern strongholds, retaining international recognition until 2001. \n\n Status: Sovereign state and government-in-exile; Capital: Kabul; Capital-in-exile: Taloqan and Fayzabad; Official languages: Dari and Pashto; Religion: Sunni Islam; Government: Unitary Islamic republic; Head of state: Burhanuddin Rabbani; Historical era: Afghan conflict; Established: 26 April 1992; Disestablished: 22 December 2001; Preceded by: Republic of Afghanistan; Succeeded by: Transitional Islamic State of Afghanistan; Currency: Afghan afghani

name: Federal Republic of Yugoslavia
description: The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was proclaimed on 27 April 1992 as a joint federation of Serbia and Montenegro following the violent disintegration of socialist Yugoslavia. Governed from Belgrade under the dominant influence of Slobodan Milosevic, the state faced severe United Nations economic sanctions for its role in the Croatian and Bosnian conflicts. Following the 1999 Kosovo War and the democratic election of a new leadership in 2000, the federation was restructured in 2003 into the State Union of Serbia and Montenegro. \n\n Status: Sovereign federal state; Capital and largest city: Belgrade; Official languages: Serbian; Religion: Serbian Orthodoxy; Government: Federal parliamentary republic; Head of state: Dobrica Ćosić; Legislature: Federal Assembly; Historical era: Yugoslav Wars; Established: 27 April 1992; Disestablished: 4 February 2003; Preceded by: Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia; Succeeded by: Serbia and Montenegro; Currency: Yugoslav dinar
